Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 1–2:

Explanation of the words:

"Fulfil the contracts" (awfu bil-'uqud): al-'uqud (contracts, covenants) are the pledges between the servant and the Lord, Exalted, and between the servant and his brother. Fulfilling them (al-wafa' biha) means not breaking them and not violating what they require.

Beast cattle (bahimat al-an'am): these are camels, cows and sheep.

"While you are in the state of ihram" (wa antum hurum): i.e., you are in ihram for hajj or 'umrah.

Rites of Allah (sha'a'ir Allah): plural of sha'irah, which here means the rites of hajj and 'umrah and all the markers of the religion of Allah, Exalted.

The sacred month (al-shahr al-haram): Rajab, the month of Mudar, which they used to hold in honour.

The offerings (al-hady): what is brought as an offering to the House and the Sacred Precinct from the beast cattle.

The garlands (al-qala'id): plural of qala'idah, which is what is hung on the offering (as a marker), and what a man hangs around himself of the bark of the trees of the Sacred Precinct, so that he may be safe.

Those making for the Sacred House (amin al-bayt al-haram): those who head toward it, seeking profit from trade or the good pleasure of Allah, Exalted.

"And when you have come out of ihram" (wa idha halaltum): i.e., from your ihram.

"Let not the enmity of a people lead you" (wa la yajrimannakum shana'an qawm): i.e., let not the hatred of a people lead you to transgress against them.

"Because they barred you" (an saddukum): i.e., on account of their having barred you.

Righteousness and piety (al-birr wa al-taqwa): al-birr is every act of obedience to Allah and His Messenger; al-taqwa is doing what Allah and His Messenger have commanded and abstaining from what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, (ﷺ).

Sin and transgression (al-ithm wa al-'udwan): al-ithm is all sins; al-'udwan is injustice and overstepping the limits.

Severe in punishment (shadid al-'iqab): i.e., His punishment is severe, unbearable and intolerable.

Meaning of the two verses:

The Truth, blessed and exalted, addresses His believing servants by the title of faith, saying: "O you who believe", i.e., O you who have believed in Me, My Messenger, My promise and My threat: "Fulfil the contracts", so do not undo them, and the covenants, so do not break them. Do not abandon an obligation or commit a prohibited act; do not forbid what is lawful nor make lawful what is unlawful. "The beast cattle have been made lawful for you", namely camels, cows and sheep, "except what is recited to you", and that is what comes in the verse: "Forbidden to you are carrion and blood..." [al-Ma'idah: 3], so do not make those lawful; and "hunting is forbidden to you while you are in ihram", so do not make it lawful. And submit the matter to Me; do not dispute concerning what I have made lawful and unlawful, for I judge as I will. This is what the first verse contains: "O you who believe, fulfil the contracts. The beast cattle have been made lawful for you, except what is recited to you, not permitting hunting while you are in ihram. Indeed Allah judges what He wills."

As for the second verse, it contains rulings, some of which have been abrogated in practice and some of which are muhkam (definitive) and remain in force until the Day of Judgement. The muhkam and obligatory matter is the prohibition of violating the rites of Allah, which are the markers of His religion, from among all that He has obligated, enjoined, forbidden and made unlawful. So one must not make lawful by abandoning an obligation or by committing a prohibited act, and among this are the rites of hajj and 'umrah. Among the abrogated rulings is the sacred month: fighting was forbidden in the sacred months, then this was abrogated by the saying of Allah, Exalted: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" (the verse). Also abrogated are the offerings of the polytheists and their garlands, and the polytheists themselves: they are not permitted to enter the Sacred Precinct, and their offerings are not accepted, and the wearing of the bark of the trees of the Sacred Precinct by themselves does not protect them from being killed, even if they were to hang on themselves all the trees of the Sacred Precinct. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the garlands, nor those making for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and His good pleasure." By "bounty" is meant provision through trade during hajj, and by "good pleasure" is meant what the polytheists used to seek by their pilgrimage: the pleasure of Allah, so that He would bless their provision for them and preserve them in their lives.

His saying, Exalted: "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt..." is an address to the believers, granting them permission to hunt, which had been forbidden to them while they were in ihram; He permitted it to them after their release from ihram. His saying, Exalted: "...and let not the enmity of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, lead you to transgress..." forbids His believing servants from letting the hatred of a people who barred them at Hudaybiyyah from the Sacred Mosque lead them to attack those people in a way that Allah has not permitted them, namely fighting them if they fight, and leaving them if they leave. Then He commanded them to cooperate in righteousness and piety, i.e., in performing obligations and virtues and abandoning prohibitions and vices, and forbade them to cooperate in their opposites, saying, Mighty and Majestic: "And cooperate in righteousness and piety, and do not cooperate in sin and transgression." Since piety encompasses the whole religion, in doing and in abstaining, He commanded them to it, saying: "And fear Allah" by believing in Him and His Messenger and obeying both in what is done and what is abstained from; and He warned them against neglecting His command, saying: "Indeed Allah is severe in punishment", so beware of Him by holding fast to piety.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1. The obligation to fulfil the covenants between Allah, Exalted, and the servant, and to preserve the contracts between the servant and his fellow servant, since the verse covers that.

2. The permissibility of eating the flesh of camels, cows and sheep, except carrion from them.

3. The prohibition of hunting while in ihram, and its permissibility after release from ihram; this refers to land game, not sea game.

4. The obligation to respect all the rites of the religion, by performing what is obligatory and abstaining from what is forbidden.

5. The absolute prohibition of aggression, even against a disbeliever.

6. The obligation of cooperation among believers in establishing the religion, and the prohibition of their cooperating to undermine it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 3:

Explanation of the words:

Al-maytah (carrion): that which dies of a beast of cattle by itself, i.e., without proper slaughter (tadhkiyah, ritual slaughter).

Wa ma uhilla li-ghayr Allah bihi (and that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked): i.e., that over which the name of other than Allah the Exalted has been mentioned, such as the Messiah, a saint (wali), or an idol.

Al-munkhaniqah (the strangled): i.e., that which died by a rope or the like.

Al-mawqudhah (the beaten to death): i.e., that which was struck with a stick or a stone and died from it.

Al-mutaraddiyah (the fallen): that which fell from a height to a lower place, such as a roof, a wall, or a mountain, and died.

Al-nati'ah (the gored): that which died because another animal gored it with its horns or head.

Wa ma akala al-sabu' (and that which a beast of prey has eaten): i.e., that which was eaten by the wolf or other predatory animals.

Illa ma dhakkaytum (except what you have slaughtered): i.e., you reached it while the soul was still settled in it, and you slaughtered it by cutting the throat or the neck.

Wa ma dhubiha 'ala al-nusub (and that which is sacrificed on stone altars): i.e., that which was slaughtered on idols that represent a god, a leader, or a great figure. Similar to them is what is slaughtered at the shrines and graves of the saints and for the jinn.

Wa an tastaqsimu bi-al-azlam (and that you seek decision by divining arrows): i.e., forbidden to you is what you obtain by seeking decisions through the arrows. Similar to this is what is taken by the soothsayer, the fortune-teller, and the drawing of lots by the prophets (?). And the false amulets containing talismans and the names of jinn and demons.

Dhalikum fisq (that is defiance): i.e., what has been mentioned, from eating carrion to seeking decisions by the arrows, is a departure from the obedience of Allah the Exalted and disobedience to Him, glory be to Him.

Faman idturra (but whoever is compelled): i.e., whoever is driven by the necessity of hunger, fearing for his own life from death, there is no harm in his eating of what has been mentioned.

Fi makhmasah (in severe hunger): makhmasah is extreme hunger, to the point that the belly shrivels from lack of food.

Ghayr mutajanif li-ithm (not inclining to sin): not leaning toward sin, not desiring disobedience by eating what was eaten of the carrion; this means that he eats no more than what sustains his strength and removes the destructive danger of hunger.

Meaning of the noble verse:

This noble verse is an explanation and detailing of the words of Allah the Exalted in the first verse of this surah, which is His saying: ﴿except what is recited to you﴾, where in this verse He mentions the rest of the forbidden meats, which are ten as follows:

Carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, that which a beast of prey has eaten, and that which is sacrificed on stone altars.

His saying ﴿except what you have slaughtered﴾ means what you have reached while the soul was settled in it, so that when you slaughter it, it convulses for the slaughter and kicks with its legs; this is a sign that it was alive and that it died by slaughter.

His saying ﴿and that you seek decision by the arrows﴾ means: the seeking of decisions by the arrows is not lawful for you, nor is eating what is given as a result of it. Its reality is that in the Jahiliyyah they used to place the arrows called al-azlam (sing. zalam), which is a small spear without a head or feathers, in a bag like a pouch, on one of which was written "my Lord commands me" and on another "my Lord forbids me." Then the one seeking decision would shake them in the bag and draw one arrow. If he found written on it "my Lord commands me," he would proceed with his work, whether a journey, a marriage, a sale or a purchase; and if he found written on it "my Lord forbids me," he would abandon what he had intended to do. Then Islam came and forbade seeking decisions by the arrows and prescribed the istikharah, which is that the believer prays two units of prayer other than the obligatory ones and says: "O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and seek power by Your power, and ask You of Your great bounty, for You have power and I have none, You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O Allah, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, both soon and later, then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless it for me; and if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair, both soon and later, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, and make me content with it," and he names his need.

Then he does or abandons what he intended, and what comes to him is good, by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

His saying ﴿that is defiance﴾ means: what I have mentioned to you of what I have forbidden you to do is defiance, so leave it.

His saying ﴿Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me﴾ informs His believing servants that the disbelievers among the polytheists and others have despaired of turning you away from your religion, as was the case before the conquest of Makkah and the entry of Thaqif and Hawazin into Islam, and your victory over them in every battle that took place between you and them. Therefore, do not fear them from now on that they will be able to overpower you and return you to disbelief, but fear Me, rather, by obeying Me and My Messenger, adhering to My limits, and following My Sunnah, so that you do not expose yourselves to My wrath by the withdrawal of My bounty, for My support is for the people of obedience and My humiliation is for the people of disobedience.

His saying ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favour upon you, and approved Islam as a religion for you﴾ is His information to His believing servants of what is a bounty and favour from Him upon them. First: the perfection of the religion in all its beliefs, acts of worship, rulings and manners, to the extent that it is said this verse was revealed on the evening of the Day of Arafah in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not live after it except eighty-one nights, then Allah took him. Second: the completion of His favour upon them: He gave them security after fear, strengthened them after weakness, gave them victory and honour after subjugation and humiliation, made them masters, opened the lands for them, made their religion manifest, and removed disbelief and the disbelievers far from them; He taught them after ignorance and guided them after misguidance. This is among the favour He completed upon them. Third: His approval of Islam as a religion for them, when He sent His Messenger with it and revealed His Book in it, clarifying its beliefs and laws, and kept them away from false religions such as Judaism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism, and made them independent of them by what He approved for them, namely Islam, which rests on submission to Allah the Exalted outwardly and inwardly; and that is the ladder of ascent to perfections and the stairway to every virtue, excellence and happiness. So to Allah belongs all praise, and to Him is the favour.

His saying ﴿But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, not inclining to sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He, the Exalted, means: whoever is compelled, i.e., compelled by necessity, which is severe hunger, which is makhmasah and musbighah, to eat what He has forbidden you from carrion and its kinds, and he eats, there is no sin upon him, for indeed I am Forgiving to My believing servants and Merciful to them. Except if he has eaten from carrion and its kinds deliberately, intending disobedience, inclining toward it, indifferent to My prohibition of it, then that is one who disobeyed Me and exposed himself to My wrath and punishment; if he repents, then I am Forgiving and Merciful, but if he persists, then My punishment is painful and severe.

Guidance of the verse

From the guidance of the verse:

1- The prohibition of carrion and what is mentioned with it, which are ten of the forbidden things.

2- The prohibition of seeking decisions by the arrows, and similar to it the drawing of lots by the prophets, the sand-divination, soothsaying and the like.

3- The prohibition of slaughtering at graves, domes and commemorative monuments, which is from shirk.

4- The permissibility of eating what a Muslim reaches alive from lawful animals and slaughters, even if it has been wounded, broken, or brought near death by any fatal cause.

5- The obligation to fear Allah the Exalted and the prohibition of fearing the disbelievers.

6- The prohibition of innovation in religion and the prohibition of legislation that contradicts the Islamic Shari'ah.

7- The permissibility of the compelled person eating carrion, being one who suffers harm from severe hunger and fears death for himself, on condition that he does not intend disobedience or incline toward sin.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 4–5:

Explanation of the words:

al-Tayyibat (the good things): what Allah the Exalted has permitted to eat and made lawful for His believing servants.

al-Jawarih (the trained hunting animals): plural of jariha, meaning one that earns (kasiba), from jaraha meaning "to earn" (takassaba).

Mukallibin (those who send them forth): meaning sending the hunting animal upon the game, whether the animal is a dog or a bird.

Ta'am alladhina utu al-kitab (the food of those given the Book): the slaughtered animals of the Jews and Christians.

Al-muhsanat (the chaste): plural of muhsana, meaning the chaste free women.

Ujurahunna (their wages): their dowries and their bridal gifts.

Ghayra musafihin (not fornicating openly): not openly committing adultery.

Akhdan (secret lovers): plural of khidn, meaning the close friend and the secret companion.

Wa man yakfur bil-iman (whoever disbelieves in faith): meaning whoever apostatizes from faith; the ba' here means "an" (from), as one says "irtadda 'an kadhha" (he turned away from such-and-such)...

Habita 'amaluhu (his deeds are nullified): all the good deeds he has done are void, so he is not rewarded for them.

Meaning of the two verses:

It was narrated that Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked permission to enter, and the Prophet (ﷺ) gave him permission, but he refused to enter because there was a small dog in the house. He said: "We do not enter a house in which there is a dog." Then the Prophet commanded that the dogs be killed, and they were killed. Then some people came asking what was lawful for them of the dog species, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are made lawful for you﴾, which means everything that is pleasant and good of what Allah the Exalted has permitted and not forbidden. And He made lawful for you also the game caught by what you have trained of the trained hunting animals, which are the dogs specially trained for hunting, as well as leopards, panthers, and birds such as falcons and the like. ﴿Mukallibin﴾ means sending them forth upon the game so that they hold it for you. ﴿You teach them of what Allah has taught you﴾, meaning you train those hunting animals with the training that Allah the Exalted has taught you. The sign of a trained hunting animal is that when it is sent forth upon the game it goes to it, when it is restrained it stops, and when it is called it responds. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾ indicates two conditions for the lawfulness of the game in addition to the animal being trained: first, that the name of Allah is mentioned when the animal is sent, by saying, for example, "In the name of Allah, bring it"; and second, that the animal does not eat from it. If it eats from it, then it has held for itself and not for the one who sent it. The exception is if it reaches the prey alive and it dies not, and then it is slaughtered; in that case it becomes lawful by the slaughter, not by the hunting. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ is a warning to whoever does not fear Allah regarding the eating of what is forbidden to eat, such as carrion and its kinds, and game caught by a trained animal that is not trained, or game caught by a trained animal that ate from it and then died before slaughter. Let him therefore fear the punishment of Allah in this, for Allah is swift in reckoning.

This is what the first verse [4] indicates. As for the second verse [5], which is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾, meaning on this day in which Allah the Exalted has perfected the religion for you, the good things, all of them, have been made lawful for you, which you asked about; likewise the food of those given the Book before you, namely the Jews and Christians specifically, so their food, meaning their slaughtered animals, is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them, meaning there is no harm in your feeding them from your food, for that is permitted for you and for them.

And He has also made lawful for you the marriage of the chaste, meaning the chaste believing women, and the chaste women from among those given the Book before you, namely the chaste Jewish and Christian women, on condition that you give them their wages, meaning their dowries, while you are muhsinin, meaning contracting marriage with them through the marriage contract that depends on the dowry, the guardian, the witnesses, and the formula of offer and acceptance; not musafihin, by giving the woman a fee for intercourse only without a contract fulfilling its conditions; nor takers of secret lovers, by marrying them secretly on the basis of companionship, friendship, and affection, for that is fornication, and it is not lawful for a fee or without a fee. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deeds have become void, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers﴾ contains an indication that permitting the forbidden and boldness in it may lead to disbelief. Whoever disbelieves after his faith, his deeds have become void, meaning the reward for what he did in Islam is nullified, even if he returns to Islam; he has only what he does after his return to Islam. And if he dies before returning to Islam, he is certainly in the Hereafter among the losers, by being cast into the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The legitimacy of asking one who does not know about what he ought to know.

2- The lawfulness of game if its conditions are met: that the hunting animal be trained, that the name of Allah the Exalted be mentioned when it is sent, and that the animal not eat from it. It is permissible to eat what is hunted with a bullet or a sharp instrument, on condition that the name of Allah is mentioned at the time of shooting, even if it is found dead without having been slaughtered.

3- The permissibility of the food and slaughtered animals of the People of the Book.

4- The permissibility of marrying women of the Book, on condition that she is free and chaste, and that the valid legal contract is concluded on her, which rests on the guardian, the witnesses, the dowry, and the formula, by the suitor saying to the guardian or agent of the woman he is proposing to: "Marry me to so-and-so," and he replies: "I have married her to you."

5- The prohibition of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah) and of secret companionship and special friendship marriage.

6- Sins may lead to disbelief.

7- The apostate from Islam, his deeds are nullified; if he returns to Islam, he is not rewarded for what he did before apostasy, and if he dies before returning to Islam, he has lost himself and his family on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the manifest loss.

Then some people came asking what was lawful for them of the dog species, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are made lawful for you﴾, which means everything that is pleasant and good of what Allah the Exalted has permitted and not forbidden. And He made lawful for you also the game caught by what you have trained of the trained hunting animals, which are the dogs specially trained for hunting, as well as leopards, panthers, and birds such as falcons and the like. ﴿Mukallibin﴾ means sending them forth upon the game so that they hold it for you. ﴿You teach them of what Allah has taught you﴾, meaning you train those hunting animals with the training that Allah the Exalted has taught you. The sign of a trained hunting animal is that when it is sent forth upon the game it goes to it, when it is restrained it stops, and when it is called it responds. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So eat of what they hold for you, and mention the name of Allah over it﴾ indicates two conditions for the lawfulness of the game in addition to the animal being trained: first, that the name of Allah is mentioned when the animal is sent, by saying, for example, "In the name of Allah, bring it"; and second, that the animal does not eat from it. If it eats from it, then it has held for itself and not for the one who sent it. The exception is if it reaches the prey alive and it dies not, and then it is slaughtered; in that case it becomes lawful by the slaughter, not by the hunting. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ is a warning to whoever does not fear Allah regarding the eating of what is forbidden to eat, such as carrion and its kinds, and game caught by a trained animal that is not trained, or game caught by a trained animal that ate from it and then died before slaughter. Let him therefore fear the punishment of Allah in this, for Allah is swift in reckoning.

This is what the first verse [4] indicates. As for the second verse [5], which is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Today the good things have been made lawful for you﴾, meaning on this day in which Allah the Exalted has perfected the religion for you, the good things, all of them, have been made lawful for you, which you asked about; likewise the food of those given the Book before you, namely the Jews and Christians specifically, so their food, meaning their slaughtered animals, is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them, meaning there is no harm in your feeding them from your food, for that is permitted for you and for them.

And He has also made lawful for you the marriage of the chaste, meaning the chaste believing women, and the chaste women from among those given the Book before you, namely the chaste Jewish and Christian women, on condition that you give them their wages, meaning their dowries, while you are muhsinin, meaning contracting marriage with them through the marriage contract that depends on the dowry, the guardian, the witnesses, and the formula of offer and acceptance; not musafihin, by giving the woman a fee for intercourse only without a contract fulfilling its conditions; nor takers of secret lovers, by marrying them secretly on the basis of companionship, friendship, and affection, for that is fornication, and it is not lawful for a fee or without a fee. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deeds have become void, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers﴾ contains an indication that permitting the forbidden and boldness in it may lead to disbelief. Whoever disbelieves after his faith, his deeds have become void, meaning the reward for what he did in Islam is nullified, even if he returns to Islam; he has only what he does after his return to Islam. And if he dies before returning to Islam, he is certainly in the Hereafter among the losers, by being cast into the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The legitimacy of asking one who does not know about what he ought to know.

2- The lawfulness of game if its conditions are met: that the hunting animal be trained, that the name of Allah the Exalted be mentioned when it is sent, and that the animal not eat from it. It is permissible to eat what is hunted with a bullet or a sharp instrument, on condition that the name of Allah is mentioned at the time of shooting, even if it is found dead without having been slaughtered.

3- The permissibility of the food and slaughtered animals of the People of the Book.

4- The permissibility of marrying women of the Book, on condition that she is free and chaste, and that the valid legal contract is concluded on her, which rests on the guardian, the witnesses, the dowry, and the formula, by the suitor saying to the guardian or agent of the woman he is proposing to: "Marry me to so-and-so," and he replies: "I have married her to you."

5- The prohibition of temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah) and of secret companionship and special friendship marriage.

6- Sins may lead to disbelief.

7- The apostate from Islam, his deeds are nullified; if he returns to Islam, he is not rewarded for what he did before apostasy, and if he dies before returning to Islam, he has lost himself and his family on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the manifest loss.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 5, verses 6–7:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**﴿إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة﴾**: i.e., when you intend to stand for the prayer (*salah*) while you are *muhdithun*, meaning without wudu' (ritual ablution).

**﴿فاغسلوا وجوهكم﴾**: i.e., after washing the two hands three times, and rinsing the mouth (*madmadah*), sniffing water into the nose (*istinshaq*), and blowing it out (*istinthar*), three times each, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained.

**﴿وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين﴾**: i.e., wash your feet up to the ankles, except when one is wearing a covering leather sock (*khuff*). In that case it is permitted to wipe over it without needing to remove it and wash the feet. This applies if one put it on after being in a state of wudu', and no more than one day and night has passed since putting it on for a resident, or three days for a traveller. This is what the Sunnah has brought.

**﴿وإن كنتم جنباً﴾**: The *junub* is one upon whom *janabah* (ritual impurity from sexual intercourse or emission of semen) has befallen. It consists of two things: the glans of the male organ disappearing into the vagina, and the emission of semen with pleasure, whether in sleep or while awake.

**﴿فاطهروا﴾**: i.e., perform the ghusl (full bathing), which is washing the whole body with water.

**﴿الغائط﴾**: a metaphor for what comes out of one of the two passages: dung, wind, or flatulence, or urine or *madhi* (pre-seminal fluid).

**﴿أو لامستم النساء﴾**: Touching women is a metaphor for sexual intercourse. Likewise, whoever touches a woman for the sake of pleasure, or touches her without intending pleasure but feels pleasure, has broken his wudu'. From this is touching the private part with the hand, because it is a likely cause of pleasure. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among you touches his private part with his hand, let him perform wudu'."

**﴿فتيمموا صعيداً﴾**: intend to use earth, or stone, or sand, or saline ground, of what rises up on the surface of the earth.

**﴿الحرج﴾**: hardship, difficulty, and constraint.

**﴿ميثاقه﴾**: i.e., the covenant of Allah the Exalted, His firm pledge. What is meant here is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, for by it the obligation to all the legal duties (*taklif shar'i*) becomes binding.

**Meaning of the two verses:**

The Lord the Exalted calls out to His believing servants, who believe in Him, His Messenger, His promise and His threat, in order to command them to purity (*taharah*) when they intend to pray. Prayer is the servant's intimate conversation with his Lord, as in the hadith: "The one who prays is conversing with his Lord." He explained to them the minor purity, which is wudu', and the major purity, which is ghusl. He also explained what substitutes for them when water, by which purity is achieved, cannot be found or they are unable to use it, and that is tayammum (dry ablution). So He the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, when you intend to stand for the prayer, wash your faces﴾. The limit of the face in length is from the place where hair grows at the top of the forehead to the end of the chin at the bottom of the face, and in width from the hinge of the right ear to the hinge of the left ear. ﴿And your hands up to the elbows﴾, so washing includes the two hands and forearms up to the beginning of the upper arms, and so the elbows are included in the washing. ﴿And wipe your heads﴾. The wording admits of both the whole and a part. The Sunnah has explained that the one wiping brings his hands forward and back, so that he wipes his whole head. This is the most complete way, and it is done with moisture on the palms. The Sunnah also showed the wiping of the ears, outer and inner, after wiping the head. ﴿And your feet up to the ankles﴾, i.e., wash your feet up to the ankles, which are the two bones protruding at the beginning of the shin. The Sunnah has shown the concession of wiping over the two leather socks in place of washing the feet, as it has shown the washing of the hands, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, and blowing it out. It has also shown that washing three times each is recommended (*mustahabb*), and that saying "In the name of Allah" at the beginning, i.e., at the start of wudu', is recommended.

The Sunnah has also shown the obligation of order (*tartib*) among the parts washed, first to last, and the obligation of continuity (*fawr*), so that no time is allowed to pass between the parts of wudu' while washing them. Rather, one does them at one time if possible. It has also emphasized the obligation of intention (*niyyah*), to the extent that it is as if it were a condition for the validity of wudu'.

He the Exalted also said: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves﴾, i.e., if one of you is afflicted with janabah, which is sexual intercourse or wet dreams. Whoever has intercourse with his wife, inserting his male organ into her private part, even if he does not ejaculate, i.e., semen does not come out of him, has become junub. Likewise, whoever has a wet dream and semen comes out of him has become junub. Indeed, everyone from whom semen comes out with pleasure, in sleep or while awake, has become junub. The cessation of a woman's menstrual blood and postpartum bleeding is like janabah, and ghusl is obligatory for it. His saying ﴿then purify yourselves﴾ means: perform ghusl. The Sunnah has explained the manner of ghusl, which is that the person intends in his heart to lift the major ritual impurity, washes his palms saying "In the name of Allah," washes his private parts and what is around them, then performs the minor wudu' that is well known, then passes wet fingers through the roots of his scalp hair, then washes his head three times, then pours water over the right side of his body, all of it, from its top to its bottom, then the left side. He takes care with the places where water may not reach, so he does not leave them unwashed, such as the navel, the armpits, and the folds (*rafghain*), which are the junctions of the thighs. And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And if you are sick, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water﴾. In this noble sentence He the Exalted mentioned the things that nullify wudu' and the circumstances that require moving from wudu' to tayammum. So He said: ﴿And if you are sick﴾. The sick person may be unable to perform wudu' because his body is weak and he cannot move, or he may have wounds or boils, with which the use of water is impossible, as the illness increases when water touches it. His saying ﴿or on a journey﴾, since travel is a likely cause of not finding water. These are the circumstances that require moving from wudu' to tayammum. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women﴾.

In the first clause He mentioned, in summary, the things that nullify wudu', which are what comes out of the two passages: dung, wind, flatulence, urine and *madhi*. He referred to them with His saying ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾, which is the place of defecation and urination. He also mentioned the cause requiring ghusl, which is intercourse, and referred to it by "touching," teaching His believing servants refined manners in their speech. His saying ﴿and you find no water﴾: for wudu' or ghusl, after you have sought it and not found it, then perform tayammum. Intend (*iqsad*, from *amma al-shay'* when one intends it) a clean earth. He means what rises upon the surface of the earth from its parts, such as dust, sand, saline ground, and stones. His saying ﴿clean﴾ means pure from impurity and filth. His saying ﴿then wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾ explains the manner of tayammum, which is that the person intends clean dust, and if that is impossible, then whatever of the parts of the earth is available to him. He strikes the earth with his palms and wipes with them his face and his hands, outer and inner, one time. His saying the Exalted ﴿with it﴾ means from that earth. With this, the Exalted explained the manner of tayammum, which is the one the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught 'Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him).

His saying the Exalted: ﴿Allah does not intend to place upon you any hardship﴾. He the Exalted informs us that He commands us to purity in its two divisions: the minor, which is wudu', and the major, which is ghusl, and what substitutes for them when one is unable, which is tayammum. He does not intend by this to put us in constraint and distress. Rather, He the Exalted intends by it to purify us from minor and major impurities and from sins, because wudu' is an expiation for the sins of the one who performs it, as its explanation has come in the Sunnah. This is His saying: ﴿But He wishes to purify you and to complete His favour upon you﴾, i.e., by guiding you to Islam and teaching you its laws, thereby preparing you for His thanks, which is obedience to Him by acting upon what Islam has brought, both inward and outward deeds. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾.

This is what the first verse [6] indicates. As for the last verse [7], which is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And remember Allah's favour upon you and His covenant which He made with you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, He the Exalted commands His believing servants to remember His favour upon them by guiding them to faith, so that they may thank Him by submitting to Islam, and to remember His covenant with which He bound them, which is the pledge a believer makes to his Lord the Exalted, by committing himself to obey Him and obey His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), when he pledges that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. As for His saying ﴿when you said, "We hear and we obey"﴾, the Companions said it verbally when they gave the pledge (*bay'ah*) to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey in ease and in hardship. And every Muslim has said it through the language of his state when he bore witness to Allah's oneness and to the Prophet's messengership. His saying the Exalted ﴿and fear Allah﴾ is a command to taqwa (God-consciousness), which is adherence to the Shari'ah and carrying it out in belief, worship, judgement and conduct. His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾ reminds them of Allah's knowledge of the hidden matters of their affairs, so that they may be watchful of Him and fear Him in secret and in public. This is part of the upbringing (*tarbiyah*) of Allah the Exalted for His believing servants, to perfect and make them happy. To Him belongs all praise, and to Him belongs grace.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The command to purity, and an explanation of how to perform wudu', how to perform ghusl, and how to perform tayammum.

2- An explanation of the excuses that transfer the believer from wudu' to tayammum.

3- An explanation of what makes wudu' and ghusl obligatory.

4- Gratitude is the cause of bounty.

5- Mentioning covenants helps one to fulfil them and to keep them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 8–11:

Explanation of the words:

Qawwamina lillah (قوامين لله): plural of qawwam, one who stands firmly for Allah, frequently fulfilling His rights and what is due to Him, and also the rights of others, neglecting nothing of that.

Shuhada' bil-qist (شهداء بالقسط): plural of shahid, meaning witness; qist means justice.

Wa la yajrimannakum (ولا يجرمنكم): meaning, let them not lead you (to do something).

Shana'an (شنآن): hatred and enmity.

Al-'adl (العدل): the opposite of injustice (jawr), namely equality without partiality or oppression.

Huwa aqrabu lil-taqwa (هو أقرب للتقوى): that is, justice is closer to God-consciousness (taqwa) than injustice is.

Hamma qawm (همّ قوم): they intended and resolved to carry out their will; the people here are the Jews of Banu al-Nadir.

Yabsutu ilaykum aydiyahum (يبسطوا إليكم إيديهم): that is, to kill your Prophet ﷺ.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to direct and guide the believers toward what perfects and makes them happy. In verse [8], Allah commands the believers to be those who stand firmly for Allah in all the rights He has over them of acts of obedience, and to be witnesses for justice, neither showing partiality nor acting unjustly in anything, whether the one testified against is a friend or an enemy. He forbids them to let the hatred or enmity of a people lead them to abandon justice, which they have been commanded to uphold. Then He commands them to be just and informs them that the people of justice are the closest of people to God-consciousness, because whoever has the habit of justice as a trait is more able to fulfil rights and obligations, to abandon wrongdoing and to avoid what is forbidden. **Explanation of the words:**

*al-Mithaq* (the covenant): the binding pledge confirmed by oaths.

*Bani Isra'il*: the Jews.

*Naqiban* (a chieftain): the *naqib* of a people is the one who looks into their affairs, investigates their conditions, and takes charge of their matters.

*Wa-'azzartumuhum*: that is, you supported them and defended them, honouring them.

*Wa-aqraḍtum Allah*: that is, you spent in His cause, hoping for His reward for your expenditure in His cause.

*La-ukaffiranna 'ankum sayyi'atikum*: I will conceal them and not hold you accountable for them.

*Laqad ḍalla sawa' al-sabil*: he has strayed from the right path, the path of guidance by which the one who follows it attains success, gaining what is loved and being saved from what is feared.

**The meaning of the noble verse:**

When Allah, exalted is He, demanded that the believers fulfil their pledges and adhere to their covenants, He reminded them in this verse of the covenant taken from the Children of Israel, which they broke, thereby deserving the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. This is meant as a lesson for the believers, so that they do not break their pledges or violate their covenant. It also serves to refute those who regard as monstrous the treachery of the Jews and their plotting to kill the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾, namely His words "Indeed I am with you", which follow. ﴿And We appointed from among them twelve chieftains﴾, that is, from each of their twelve tribes a chieftain who would oversee them and inquire into their conditions as a leader among them. These were the ones whom Moses, peace be upon him, sent to Palestine to become acquainted with the conditions of the Canaanites before fighting them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I am with you﴾, and this is the clause of the covenant: ﴿If you establish prayer (salah)﴾, that is, by My might and majesty, ﴿if you establish prayer, give zakah (obligatory alms), believe in My messengers﴾, affirming them in what they brought you, ﴿and support them﴾ by aiding and honouring them, ﴿and lend Allah a goodly loan﴾, that is, in addition to the obligatory zakah, spending generously and purifying the soul through faith and righteous deeds. ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds﴾ by eliminating their traces from your souls until they become pure and clean, ﴿and I will surely admit you﴾ after that purification ﴿to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, that is, beneath their trees and palaces, ﴿the rivers﴾. This is the reward for fulfilling the covenant. ﴿But whoever disbelieves﴾ after that, by breaking the covenant, neglecting what it contains and disbelieving after it, ﴿has certainly strayed from the right way﴾, that is, has missed the path of success in this world and the Hereafter, having departed from the path that leads its follower to salvation and happiness.

**Guidance from the verse:**

1. The exhortation to fulfil legal obligations.
2. The refutation of the astonishment and amazement of those who wonder at the Jews' deceit, treachery and wickedness, and who regard such conduct from them as monstrous.
3. Establishing prayer, giving zakah, and spending in the cause of Allah, which Allah ordained for this Ummah as acts of worship, just as He ordained them for earlier nations.
4. The obligation to honour the Messenger (ﷺ) and to support him, his community and his religion.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 13–14:

Explanation of the words:

Naqd al-mithaq (breaking the covenant): violating it by not adhering to what it contains of commands and prohibitions.

La'annahum (We cursed them): We expelled them from the causes of mercy and the requirements of honour and perfection.

Yuharrifun al-kalim (they distort the words): they alter speech and twist its meanings for corrupt purposes; al-kalim (the words) is the plural of kalam (speech).

Wa nasu hazzan mimma dhukiru bih (and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of): they abandoned a great share of what Allah, exalted is He, had reminded them of, i.e., what He had commanded them in their Book.

KhA'ina (treacherous): treachery, or a treacherous group among them.

Fa'fu 'anhum wa asfah (so pardon them and overlook): i.e., do not hold them to account, and turn your face away from them, doing good to them by this.

Inna nasara (we are Christians): i.e., they innovated the innovation of Christianity, saying "we are Christians."

Aghrayna baynahum al-'adawa (We have stirred up enmity among them): al-Ighra' (stirring up) means inciting and provoking; the meaning is that We created for them causes of division and discord until the Day of Resurrection, by Our special arrangement, so they are perpetually enemies of one another.

Meaning of the two verses:

The noble context continues to explain the wickedness and treachery of the Jews. In this noble verse [13], Allah, exalted is He, informs that the Jews, whose covenant Allah took in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, to act upon what is in the Torah, to fight the Canaanites and expel them from the land of Jerusalem, and from whom He raised twelve leaders, broke their covenant and violated their pledge. For this, He cursed them and made their hearts hard, so they distort words from their places. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, i.e., because of their breaking of the covenant taken from them to act upon what is in the Torah and obey their messenger, ﴿We cursed them﴾, i.e., We removed them from the circle of mercy and the abundance of good and peace, ﴿and made their hearts hard﴾, harsh and rough, not softened by admonition and not yielding to acceptance of guidance. ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, so they put forward and put back, delete parts of speech, and twist its meanings to suit their desires. Among this is their interpretation of the verses indicating the prophethood of both Jesus and Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, in the Torah. ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, and they abandoned much of what they were commanded with of the laws and rulings, turning away from them and feigning forgetfulness of them, as if they had never been commanded with them. Is it then surprising from one whose condition is this—treachery, breaking, and betrayal? And you, O our Messenger, will not cease to ﴿discover treachery from them﴾, i.e., a treacherous group among them, like the treachery of the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿except for a few of them﴾, for they do not betray, like 'Abdullah ibn Salam and others. On the basis of this, ﴿so pardon them﴾, do not hold them accountable by killing, ﴿and overlook﴾ them, not confronting what they dislike, so do good to them by this, ﴿indeed Allah loves the doers of good﴾.

This is what the first verse [13] indicates. As for the second verse [14], in this context, Allah, exalted is He, informs about the Christians and that their condition is like the condition of the Jews, not differing much from them. We took their covenant to believe in Me and My messengers and to act upon My law, but they abandoned much of what the covenant and pledge were taken from them, forgetting it. Thus We stirred up enmity and hatred among them as a fruit of their breaking of the covenant, so each group became zealous for its own opinion, disputes erupted among them, and argument multiplied. From this arose enmity and hatred, which will continue until the Day of Resurrection. Allah, exalted is He, will inform them of what they used to do of falsehood, evil, and corruption, and will recompense them with a recompense corresponding to the wickedness of their souls and the badness of their deeds, for indeed your Lord is Mighty and Wise.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of breaking covenants and violating pledges, especially those between the servant and his Lord.

2- Treachery is a characteristic inseparable from most Jews; few of them are free from this trait.

3- The recommendation of pardon when one has the ability, and it is one of the qualities of the righteous.

4- The condition of the Christians does not differ much from the condition of the Jews, as if they drank from one water. Therefore, evil from them is not surprising, and they cannot be trusted with a secret; they are mutually cooperative and mutually counselling in enmity toward Islam and in waging war against it.

In this noble verse [13], Allah, exalted is He, informs that the Jews, whose covenant Allah took in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, to act upon what is in the Torah, to fight the Canaanites and expel them from the land of Jerusalem, and from whom He raised twelve leaders, broke their covenant and violated their pledge. For this, He cursed them and made their hearts hard, so they distort words from their places. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾, i.e., because of their breaking of the covenant taken from them to act upon what is in the Torah and obey their messenger, ﴿We cursed them﴾, i.e., We removed them from the circle of mercy and the abundance of good and peace, ﴿and made their hearts hard﴾, harsh and rough, not softened by admonition and not yielding to acceptance of guidance. ﴿They distort words from their places﴾, so they put forward and put back, delete parts of speech, and twist its meanings to suit their desires. Among this is their interpretation of the verses indicating the prophethood of both Jesus and Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace, in the Torah. ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾, and they abandoned much of what they were commanded with of the laws and rulings, turning away from them and feigning forgetfulness of them, as if they had never been commanded with them. Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The prohibition of breaking covenants and violating pledges, especially those between the servant and his Lord.

2- Treachery is a characteristic inseparable from most Jews; few of them are free from this trait.

3- The recommendation of pardon when one has the ability, and it is one of the qualities of the righteous.

4- The condition of the Christians does not differ much from the condition of the Jews, as if they drank from one water. Therefore, evil from them is not surprising, and they cannot be trusted with a secret; they are mutually cooperative and mutually counselling in enmity toward Islam and in waging war against it.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 5, verses 15–16:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book): here they are the Jews and the Christians together.

*Qadja'akum rasuluna* (Our Messenger has certainly come to you): Muhammad (ﷺ).

*Tukhfuna min al-Kitab* (you conceal of the Book): the Book here refers to the Torah and the Gospel. What they conceal are the attributes of the Prophet (ﷺ) and some rulings. Those who oppose these rulings deny them out of fear of disgrace, such as stoning, for example.

*Wa ya'fu 'an kathir* (and He overlooks much): He does not mention it to you, since there is no benefit in mentioning it.

*Nur wa Kitab mubin* (a light and a clear Book): the light is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the Book is the noble Qur'an.

*Ila sirat mustaqim* (to a straight path): Islam, which is the true religion, without which there is no salvation. "Straight" means that there is no crookedness in it.

**The meaning of the two verses:**

The context is still concerning the People of the Book. After Allah, the Exalted, explained their falsehood and the evil and wrongdoing they were upon, He called them, while He is their Lord and more merciful to them than they are to themselves, to the path of their salvation and perfection. He called them to believe in His Messenger and His Book, the Messenger whom no one has followed without being rewarded, and the Book whom no one has taken as a guide and then gone astray or become wretched. He said: ﴿O People of the Book, certainly there has come to you Our Messenger﴾, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿making clear to you much﴾ through Our revelation ﴿of what you have been concealing from the Scripture and overlooking much﴾ of the matters of the Law and religion that you conceal out of fear of exposure, because it is truth that you have denied. This includes the descriptions and attributes of the unlettered Prophet, so that people will not believe in him, and the ruling of stoning in the Torah, and similar things. ﴿And He overlooks much﴾, leaving aside what is not mentioned because there is no reason to mention it. ﴿O People of the Book, there has certainly come to you from Allah, your Lord, a light﴾, which is Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and a clear Book﴾, which is the Qur'an, since it makes clear everything of the matters of religion and worldly affairs, and everything upon which human happiness and perfection in this world and the Hereafter depend. ﴿Allah guides thereby﴾, the Exalted, ﴿whoever follows His pleasure﴾, and this is by sincere desire to obtain the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through doing what He loves and abandoning what displeases Him, in every belief, saying and action, ﴿to the ways of peace﴾, that is, the paths of happiness and perfection. ﴿And brings them﴾, that is, those who follow Allah's pleasure, ﴿out of darknesses﴾, which are the darknesses of disbelief, polytheism and doubt, ﴿into the light by His permission﴾, to the light of correct faith and correct worship that purifies the soul and refines the conscience through feeling His success and help, the Exalted. ﴿And guides them﴾, that is, those who truly desire Allah's pleasure, ﴿to a straight path﴾, with which they will never go astray nor be wretched, and which is His true religion, Islam, which He does not accept any religion other than. Whoever turns away from it is not guided, nor is he made happy, nor perfected.

**Lessons of the two verses:**

1. Allah's sincere counsel to the People of the Book is to call them to the ways of peace by entering Islam.
2. The denial by Jews and Christians of many legal rulings and proofs of Muhammad's prophethood is shown, through deceit and envy, so that people will not believe in Islam and enter it.
3. Following the Prophetic Sunnah guides its follower to his happiness and perfection.
4. The Qur'an is a proof upon all people, due to its clarification of the truth in everything.
5. Whoever seeks Allah's pleasure with sincerity attains every good and is safe from every harm.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 17–19:

Explanation of the words:

Laqad kafara alladhina (﴿Certainly those have disbelieved﴾): because they denied the truth and said, falsely, "God is the Messiah, son of Maryam."

Al-Masih (the Messiah): a title for ʿIsa ibn Maryam, the servant and messenger of God, peace be upon him.

Maryam (Mary): daughter of ʿImran, one of the righteous women of the Children of Israel, and mother of ʿIsa, peace be upon him.

Yuhlik (﴿destroy﴾): causes to die and annihilates.

Qadir (﴿All-Powerful﴾): able to bring into existence and to annihilate everything He wills to bring into existence or annihilate.

Al-ahibba' (﴿beloved ones﴾): the singular is habib, just as the plural of ibn (son) is abna'.

ʿAla fatra (﴿after a gap﴾): al-fatra is the period during which revelation ceases because God, exalted is He, has sent no messenger.

Bashir wa nadhir (﴿a bringer of good news and a warner﴾): al-bashir is the one who gives good tidings of good, and al-nadhir is the one who warns against evil. He is the Messenger of God ﷺ, who gives good news to the believers and warns the disbelievers.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of the People of the Book. In the first verse [17], God, exalted is He, informs them, emphasizing the report with an oath that is omitted but indicated by the lam that falls in the answer to the oath, saying: ﴿Certainly those have disbelieved who said, "Indeed, God is the Messiah, son of Maryam."﴾ The reason for their disbelief is that they made the created, the one who is sustained, to be God, the Creator and Lord of everything. This is one of the most abominable kinds of disbelief. And although this was not the statement of most Christians, by their affiliation with Christianity, their adherence to it, and their entry into the ranks of its principles and teachings, they are held accountable for it, because approval of disbelief is disbelief.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Who then has any power against God at all?"﴾ teaches His Messenger how to argue against the people of this falsehood, so He says to him: Say to them, "Who has any power against God if He wills to destroy the Messiah, son of Maryam, and his mother, peace be upon them both, and everyone on earth entirely?" The answer, decisively, is no one. So how can the servant of God be God, or a god alongside God? Is this not plain error and the bewilderment of minds in its perfection? Then God, exalted is He, informs that to Him belongs ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾, in creation and in disposal, and that He ﴿creates what He wills﴾, creating without restraint or prohibition, and He is ﴿over all things competent﴾. He created Adam from dust without father or mother, created Eve from Adam, and created ʿIsa from Maryam without a father. He creates what He wills, and He is over all things competent. Thus the fact that the Messiah, peace be upon him, was created by the word "Be" without a father does not necessitate, either rationally or by revelation, that he is God, or the son of God, or a third of three with God, as is the belief of most Christians. And it is astonishing how stubbornly they persist in this falsehood. This is what the first verse indicates.

As for the second verse [18], it contains a demonstration of the error of both the Jews and the Christians, namely their claim that they are ﴿the sons of God and His beloved﴾, for God says of them: ﴿The Jews and the Christians said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved."﴾ This is arrogance, folly, and error. So God commanded His Messenger to reply to them by saying: Say to them, O our Messenger: ﴿Why then does He punish you for your sins?﴾ Does a father punish his sons, or a beloved punish those who love him? Yet you say you will be punished in the Fire for forty days, because of the sin of your forefathers' worship of the calf, forty days, as comes in His saying, quoting them: ﴿And they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80]. The truth is that this statement of yours is among the nonsense and falsehoods on which you live. As for you, you are human beings among those whom God created; your relation to Him is the relation of a created being to a Creator and of a servant to an owner. Whoever among you believes and does righteous deeds will be forgiven and honored, and whoever among you disbelieves and does evil He will punish, as is His way with all His servants, and there is no objection to Him, for to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and you are among those He owns. To Him is the return, so you will return to Him and He will repay you according to your deeds; indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.

This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse [19], it contains the establishment of proof against the People of the Book. The Lord, blessed and exalted, addressed them saying, "O People of the Book," and informed them that His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ has come to them, making clear to them the path that saves and makes happy at one time, after a gap in messengers, since revelation had ceased since ʿIsa was raised to heaven, and about five hundred and seventy years had passed since then. We sent Our Messenger to you so that you could not say, offering excuses for your polytheism, disbelief, association of partners with God, and corruption: ﴿No bringer of good news nor warner has come to us.﴾ Behold, here is the bringer of good news, Muhammad ﷺ; so believe in him and follow him, and you will be saved and made happy. Otherwise, punishment is certain for you, and God is competent to punish you, just as He is over all things competent.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The disbelief of one who attributes to God what is far removed from Him of all deficiencies.

2- The falsehood of the claim of the Jews and Christians that they are the sons of God and His beloved, by rational proof.

3- The creatures' relation to God does not go beyond their being created by Him and owned by Him, He disposes of them as He wills and judges them as He desires.

4- Cutting off the excuse of the People of the Book by sending the Messenger Muhammad ﷺ after a gap in messengers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 20–23:

Explanation of the words:

Allah's blessing upon you: among it is their deliverance from Pharaoh and his chiefs.

When He made among you prophets: among them Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 24–26:

Explanation of the words:

*Lan nadkhuluha* (we will never enter it): that is, the city which they were ordered to attack, and to enter upon its people therein.

*Al-fasiqin* (the defiantly disobedient): that is, in disobeying the command of Allah and His Messenger by abandoning jihad out of cowardice and fear.

*Muharramatun 'alayhim* (forbidden to them): that is, a forbiddance that is cosmic and decreed (taḥrīm kawnī qaḍā'ī), not a legislated, devotional prohibition (taḥrīm shar'ī ta'abbudī).

*Yatihuna fi'l-ard* (they will wander in the land): that is, in the land of Sinai, bewildered therein, not knowing where they are going, for a period of forty years.

*Fa-la ta'sa* (so do not grieve): that is, do not be sorrowful and do not regret.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the answer of the people to the request of the two righteous men to storm the city against the enemy, for they said with utter impudence, baseness and vileness: ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it, [as long as they are in it]..."﴾ that is, the city, ﴿"...for as long as they remain therein. So go, you and your Lord, and fight..."﴾ the people of the city; "as for us, we will sit here." What greater rebellion and disobedience is there than this? What greater cowardice and weakness is there than this? What lower breach of manners is there than this? Here Moses, disassociating himself from the defiantly disobedient people, said: "My Lord," that is, O my Lord, ﴿"indeed I possess no one except myself and my brother..."﴾ meaning Harun, ﴿"...so part us from the defiantly disobedient people."﴾ Thus he sought to be absolved of them and of their conduct, since they had surely deserved punishment. So his Lord, the Exalted, answered him in the third verse [26]: ﴿"It is forbidden for them..."﴾ that is, the Holy Land, for forty years they will not enter it; and indeed they did not enter it until after the mentioned period had passed ﴿"forty years."﴾ And how were they during it? They wandered in the land of Sinai, bewildered in their journey, not knowing where they were going or from where they were coming. Accordingly, do not grieve, O our Messenger, and do not regret over the defiantly disobedient people, for this is their recompense of punishment, hastened for them; so let them taste it!!

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of the cowardice of the Jews, and their bad manners toward their Lord and their prophets.

2- The obligation of disassociating from the people of defiance by hating their deeds, and of leaving them to the wrath of Allah that is about to descend upon them.

3- The prohibition of grieving over and regretting the defiantly disobedient and the wrongdoers when divine punishment befalls them as recompense for their defiance.

**Explanation of the Words (Sharh al-Kalimat):**

*Wa-utlu 'alayhim* (And recite to them): And recite to the Jews who had planned to kill you and your companions.

*Naba'a ibnay Adam* (the story of the two sons of Adam): the account of the two sons of Adam, Habil (Abel) and Qabil (Cain).

*Qurbanan* (an offering): al-qurban (sacrificial offering) is what one draws near to God with, such as prayer and charity.

*Basatta ilayya yadaka* (you stretched out your hand toward me): you extended your hand toward me.

*An tabu'a bi-ithmi wa-ithmik* (that you bear my sin and your sin): you will return to God on the Day of Resurrection bearing the sin of killing me, and your sin of your disobedience.

*Fa-tawwaat lahu nafsuhu* (so his soul made the killing easy for him): he encouraged him to kill and made it appealing to him until he did it.

*Ghuraban* (a crow): a well-known black bird, used as a proverb for blackness.

*Yuwari sawata akhihi* (to conceal his brother's corpse): he covers his brother's body with earth. It is said that it is called *sawa'a* because people dislike looking at a dead body, and *sawa'a* is what one dislikes to look at.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The noble Qur'anic context continues to speak of the Banu al-Nadir Jews, who planned to kill the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. God says to His Messenger: recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, so that they may learn through it the outcome of the crime of murder they had planned, as a rebuke to them and a demonstration of your noble stance toward them, since you pardoned them when you had power over them and did not kill them. You were with them as the better of the two sons of Adam. ﴿...when they both offered a sacrifice...﴾, that is, each of them offered a sacrifice to God, so God accepted the sacrifice of one of them because it was from the best of his wealth and he offered it with a pleased soul. ﴿And it was not accepted from the other﴾, who was Qabil, because it was from the worst of his wealth, and his soul was attached to it. So he said to his brother Habil, "I will surely kill you," out of envy of him, just as the Jews envied you and your people for your prophethood and message. His brother said to him: the non-acceptance of your offering is due to yourself, not to anyone else. God only accepts from those who are mindful of Him, not from those who associate others with Him. Had you been mindful and avoided shirk, your offering would have been accepted, because God accepts only what is sincerely for Him, and you associated your self and your desires with your offering, so it was not accepted from you. By God, with an oath: ﴿If you stretch out your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand toward you to kill you﴾, and he gave as the reason: ﴿...Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, that I should meet Him bearing blood I shed unjustly. And if you insist on killing me, I will not kill you, because I want you to bear my sin and your sin, that is, to return to our Lord on the Day of Resurrection bearing the sin of killing me, along with your sin that you committed throughout your life, and thus because of that you will be among the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever, never departing from it. God the Exalted said: ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿So his soul made the killing of his brother easy for him﴾, that is, it encouraged him to it and made it appealing to him, so he killed him. ﴿So he became among the losers﴾, the regretful, because he did not know what to do with him. He carried him on his shoulder and walked with him until the body rotted. Then God sent a crow that searched in the earth, that is, it scratched the ground with its feet and beak and scattered dirt over a dead crow with it, until it covered it. In other words, God sent the crow to show him how to conceal, that is, cover, his brother's shame, that is, his corpse. When Qabil saw what the crow had done with its dead companion, he said, regretful and grieved: "Woe is me!", that is, "O my woe, come, for this is the time of your presence."
