Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 32:

Explanation of the words:

من أجل ذلك (min ajl dhalika): because of that, i.e., because of that killing.

كتبنا (katabna): We prescribed (lit. "wrote"); i.e., We revealed.

أو فساد في الأرض (aw fasad fi al-ard): or corruption in the land, by waging war against Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.

ومن أحياها (wa man ahyaha): and whoever preserves it, i.e., one who is able to kill him but, since he deserves it, refrains from killing him.

بالبينات (bil-bayyinat): with clear signs, i.e., clear verses carrying the laws and proofs.

لمسرفون (lamusrifun): those who are excessive, i.e., those who commit many sins and transgressions.

The meaning of the noble verse:

He, the Exalted, says: Because of the grave wickedness of the crime of killing and the immeasurable harms and corruptions that follow from it, We prescribed for the Children of Israel, because of how widespread killing and the shedding of blood had become among them, for they killed the prophets and those among the people who commanded justice, owing to this eagerness for killing. They killed two messengers, Zechariah and Yahya, and they plotted to kill each of the two great messengers, Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ). Because of this, We made the punishment severe for them: whoever among them kills a soul without a soul being taken in retribution, that is, unjustly and aggressively, or without corruption in the land that he committed, which is waging war against Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, it is as if he had killed all of mankind, meaning he will be punished with the punishment of one who has killed all of mankind on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever preserves a soul, by refraining from killing one who deserved to be killed, pardoning him and leaving him for the sake of Allah, sparing him, it is as if he had preserved all of mankind, meaning he will be given the reward of one who has preserved all of mankind. All of this Allah, the Exalted, legislated for them to deter them from the killing to which they had persisted, and to encourage them toward the pardon which they had neglected, moved away from, and never recognized. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And certainly did Our messengers come to them with clear proofs﴾ informs of their condition, consoling His Messenger Muhammad regarding the concern he bore from them, for they are the ones who conspired to kill him: the evil that clung to the Jews and the corruption that became their constant attribute, especially plotting murder and kindling the fire of war, was not out of ignorance or lack of knowledge on their part, not at all. Rather, their messengers came to them with clear signs, upright laws, and lofty morals, but they are a people of slander, rebellious against the laws, excessive in evil and corruption. Therefore, indeed, many of them are excessive in evil and corruption on the earth. With the end of this verse, and with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands against you...﴾, which is verse [11], the discussion concerning the Jews related to the incident of their intent to kill the Messenger (ﷺ) and his companions ends. It was mentioned as consolation for the Messenger of Allah and his companions, and likewise as consolation for every believer who is exposed to the plotting of the Jews, upon them be the curse of Allah.

Guidance from the verse:

From the guidance of the verse:

1- The discipline of the Lord, the Exalted, for the Children of Israel, and, regrettably, they did not benefit from it.

2- The corruption of the Children of Israel did not arise from ignorance or lack of knowledge; rather, it was following their desires and rushing after the fleeting goods of this world. Therefore Allah became angry with them and cursed them, because they knew.

3- Despite the doubling of the punishment for the crime upon the Jews, and the multiplying of the reward for good deeds for them, they are the people most excessive in evil and corruption on the earth.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 33–34:

Explanation of the words:

Yuharibuna Allah wa Rasulahu (those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger): by leaving obedience to them, bearing arms against the believers, killing them, plundering their wealth, and violating their sanctities.

Wa yas'awna fi al-ardi fasadan (and strive upon the earth in corruption): by terrifying people, cutting off their roads, plundering their wealth, and violating their honour.

Aw yusallabu (or they be crucified): they are tied to wooden poles and killed, or [they are crucified] after they have been killed.

Min khilaf (from opposite sides): that the right hand and the left foot are cut off, or the reverse.

Aw yunfau min al-ard (or they be banished from the land): that is, from the land of Islam.

Khizy fi al-dunya (disgrace in this world): humiliation and degradation.

Adhab 'azim (great punishment): the punishment of Hell.

An taqdiru 'alayhim (before you have power over them): that is, before you gain control over them, by their fleeing far away and then coming back as Muslims.

Meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned what He had obligated upon the Jews of severe punishment for the crime of killing and corruption on the earth, in order to break the sharpness of their boldness in killing and corruption, He mentioned here the ruling and recompense for those who wage war against the Muslims and strive in corruption in their lands. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the penalty of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾ by disbelief after faith, and killing and plundering after security, ﴿and strive upon the earth in corruption﴾ by terrifying the Muslims, cutting off their roads, taking their wealth, and violating their sanctities and honour, ﴿is only that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides or be banished from the land.﴾ This is what I mention to you and nothing else, so know it. The meaning of "they be killed" is: they are killed one after another, as a deterrent to them, a terror, and a discipline (ta'zir) for others. The meaning of "they be crucified" is: after one of them is killed, he is tied to a wooden post for three days. The meaning of "they be banished from the land" is: they are expelled from the abode of Islam, or sent to a remote place such as an island in a sea, or they are imprisoned until the Muslims are rid of their evil and harm. That prescribed penalty is a disgrace and humiliation for them in this world, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾, this is a connected exception from those warriors: whoever we were unable to seize and did not gain power over, and who after a period came to us repentant, his ruling differs from those before him. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ carries a clear indication of lightening the ruling upon him. If he was a disbeliever and embraced Islam, then Islam erases what was before it, so all the punishments mentioned in the verse fall from him. If he was a Muslim, then crucifixion is dropped, but he is obligated to return the wealth he took if it remains in his hand. If he killed or committed adultery and a claimant demands the establishment of the legal punishment upon him, the legal punishment is established upon him; otherwise it is left to Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Clarification of the ruling on hirabah and its reality: it is the going out of a group of two or more, who have weapons in their hands and strength, going out to the desert away from cities and villages, launching attacks on Muslims, killing, plundering, and violating honour. This is hirabah, and its people are called al-muharibun (those who wage hirabah), and their ruling is what Allah mentioned in the first verse [33].

2- The imam has discretion in imposing whichever penalty he sees as suitable for restoring security, if we say that "aw" in the verse indicates choice (takhyir). Otherwise, whoever kills and takes wealth and terrifies people is killed and crucified; whoever kills without taking wealth is killed; whoever kills and takes wealth has his right hand and left foot cut off from opposite sides; and whoever neither kills nor takes wealth is banished.

3- Whoever of the warriors repents before being seized is pardoned, unless he still has in his possession wealth he plundered, in which case he must return it to its owners, or he himself demands the establishment of the legal punishment upon him, and he is granted that.

4- The greatness of Allah's pardon and mercy toward His servants, in forgiving the one who repents and in His mercy toward him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 33–34:

Explanation of the words:

Yuharibuna Allah wa Rasulahu (those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger): by leaving obedience to them, bearing arms against the believers, killing them, plundering their wealth, and violating their sanctities.

Wa yas'awna fi al-ardi fasadan (and strive upon the earth in corruption): by terrifying people, cutting off their roads, plundering their wealth, and violating their honour.

Aw yusallabu (or they be crucified): they are tied to wooden poles and killed, or [they are crucified] after they have been killed.

Min khilaf (from opposite sides): that the right hand and the left foot are cut off, or the reverse.

Aw yunfau min al-ard (or they be banished from the land): that is, from the land of Islam.

Khizy fi al-dunya (disgrace in this world): humiliation and degradation.

Adhab 'azim (great punishment): the punishment of Hell.

An taqdiru 'alayhim (before you have power over them): that is, before you gain control over them, by their fleeing far away and then coming back as Muslims.

Meaning of the two verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned what He had obligated upon the Jews of severe punishment for the crime of killing and corruption on the earth, in order to break the sharpness of their boldness in killing and corruption, He mentioned here the ruling and recompense for those who wage war against the Muslims and strive in corruption in their lands. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the penalty of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger﴾ by disbelief after faith, and killing and plundering after security, ﴿and strive upon the earth in corruption﴾ by terrifying the Muslims, cutting off their roads, taking their wealth, and violating their sanctities and honour, ﴿is only that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides or be banished from the land.﴾ This is what I mention to you and nothing else, so know it. The meaning of "they be killed" is: they are killed one after another, as a deterrent to them, a terror, and a discipline (ta'zir) for others. The meaning of "they be crucified" is: after one of them is killed, he is tied to a wooden post for three days. The meaning of "they be banished from the land" is: they are expelled from the abode of Islam, or sent to a remote place such as an island in a sea, or they are imprisoned until the Muslims are rid of their evil and harm. That prescribed penalty is a disgrace and humiliation for them in this world, ﴿and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Fire. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾, this is a connected exception from those warriors: whoever we were unable to seize and did not gain power over, and who after a period came to us repentant, his ruling differs from those before him. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ carries a clear indication of lightening the ruling upon him. If he was a disbeliever and embraced Islam, then Islam erases what was before it, so all the punishments mentioned in the verse fall from him. If he was a Muslim, then crucifixion is dropped, but he is obligated to return the wealth he took if it remains in his hand. If he killed or committed adultery and a claimant demands the establishment of the legal punishment upon him, the legal punishment is established upon him; otherwise it is left to Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

Guidance of the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Clarification of the ruling on hirabah and its reality: it is the going out of a group of two or more, who have weapons in their hands and strength, going out to the desert away from cities and villages, launching attacks on Muslims, killing, plundering, and violating honour. This is hirabah, and its people are called al-muharibun (those who wage hirabah), and their ruling is what Allah mentioned in the first verse [33].

2- The imam has discretion in imposing whichever penalty he sees as suitable for restoring security, if we say that "aw" in the verse indicates choice (takhyir). Otherwise, whoever kills and takes wealth and terrifies people is killed and crucified; whoever kills without taking wealth is killed; whoever kills and takes wealth has his right hand and left foot cut off from opposite sides; and whoever neither kills nor takes wealth is banished.

3- Whoever of the warriors repents before being seized is pardoned, unless he still has in his possession wealth he plundered, in which case he must return it to its owners, or he himself demands the establishment of the legal punishment upon him, and he is granted that.

4- The greatness of Allah's pardon and mercy toward His servants, in forgiving the one who repents and in His mercy toward him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 35–37:

Explanation of the words:

*Ittaqu Allah* (اتقوا الله): Fear His punishment, so comply with His command and the command of His Messenger, and avoid what they both forbid.

*Wabtaghu* (وابتغوا): Seek.

*Al-wasilah* (الوسيلة): Draw near to Him by doing what He loves and abandoning what displeases Him, so that you attain nearness to Him.

*Wa-jahidu fi sabilihi* (وجاهدوا في سبيله): Strive against yourselves by compelling them to learn, act, and teach; and against His enemies by calling them to Islam and fighting them over it.

*Tuflihun* (تُفْلِحُون): You will be saved from the Fire and enter Paradise.

*Adhab muqim* (عذاب مقيم): Lasting, never ceasing or departing.

The meaning of the two verses:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, calls His believing servants who believe in Him and His Messenger, in His promise and His warning, to guide them to what saves them from punishment so that they avoid it, and to what brings them near to mercy so that they do it. He says: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means of access to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed﴾. The meaning of "fear Allah" is: fear His punishment, so obey Him by doing His commands and the commands of His Messenger, and avoiding their prohibitions, for the punishment of Allah is only guarded against by piety. The meaning of ﴿and seek the means of access to Him﴾ is: seek nearness to Him, that is, draw near to Him by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes, so that you attain nearness to Him. The meaning of ﴿and strive in His cause﴾ is: strive against yourselves in obeying Him, against Satan in disobeying him, and against the disbelievers for Islam, to bring them to Him and into His religion, expending all that is within your power of effort and capacity. This is what the first verse [35] indicates.

As for the second verse [36], which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved – even if they had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it...﴾ etc., it is the reason for what the first verse called for, namely the command to piety and seeking nearness to Allah, Exalted is He, through faith and righteous deeds. This is because the punishment from which they were commanded to guard themselves through piety is a punishment that cannot be endured at all. Consider this: those who disbelieved, ﴿even if they had all that is in the earth entirely﴾ of wealth, both silent and living, ﴿and the like of it with it﴾, and it were accepted from them as ransom for themselves from that punishment, they would offer it willingly. It is a painful punishment, extremely agonizing, and most painful in its pain. They will long with all their hearts to come out of the Fire, ﴿but they will not emerge from it, and for them is a lasting punishment﴾, enduring, never ceasing or departing.

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- The obligation of fearing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, seeking nearness to Him, and striving in His cause.

2- The legitimacy of seeking nearness to Allah through faith and righteous deeds.

3- The greatness of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection and its boundless severity.

4- There is no ransom on the Day of Resurrection, nor any intercession that benefits the disbeliever so that he emerges from the Fire through it.

5- The fine reasoning given for commands and prohibitions with what encourages compliance and abstention.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 38–40:

Explanation of the words:

Al-sariq (the male thief): the one who takes property from a protected place (hirz) secretly, the value of which is a quarter of a dinar or more.

Al-sariqa (the female thief): the one who takes property from a protected place secretly, the value of which is a quarter of a dinar or more.

Fa-iqta'u aydiyahuma (so cut off their hands): that is, cut off the hand of whichever of them steals, from the wrist (al-kū' (wrist)).

Nakalan (as a deterrent): a punishment from God that makes others shrink from stealing.

ʿAzīzun ḥakīm (Mighty, Wise): ʿAzīz (Mighty): the Overpowering, whom nothing can prevent from His will; ḥakīm (Wise): in His management and decree.

Ba'da zulmihi (after his wrongdoing): after he has wronged himself by disobeying God, by taking people's property.

Wa-aslaḥa (and reforms): that is, reforms himself by purifying it through repentance and righteous deeds.

Fa-inna Allāha yatūbu 'alayhi (then God accepts his repentance): that is, He accepts his repentance, forgives him and shows mercy to him, if He wills.

Lahu mulku al-samawati wa-al-ard (To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth): in creation, dominion and management.

Yu'adhdhibu man yashā' (He punishes whom He wills): that is, His punishment of one who dies disobedient to His command and denying His right.

Wa-yaghfiru liman yashā' (and forgives whom He wills): of those who repent of their sin and turn to Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs us, establishing a ruling of His law: that whoever steals property worth a quarter of a dinar or more from a place of its kind secretly, being sane and adult, and is brought before the ruler, and likewise the female thief, the ruling is that the right hand of the male thief is cut off at the wrist, and likewise the hand of the female thief, as recompense for them for their wrongdoing in transgressing against the property of others. ﴿A punishment from God﴾, that is, a punishment from God Almighty for them that makes others not venture to take people's property by the forbidden way of theft. ﴿And God is Mighty, Wise﴾, overpowering in His command, wise in His decree and judgment. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as recompense for what they have earned﴾ of sin, ﴿a punishment from God. And God is Mighty, Wise.﴾

As for His words, exalted is He, in the second verse [39]: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing﴾, that is, repents of theft after having wronged himself thereby, ﴿and reforms﴾ himself through repentance, and among that is returning the stolen property, ﴿then indeed God will accept his repentance﴾, for He, exalted is He, is Forgiving toward those who repent and Merciful toward the believers. As for His words, exalted is He, in the third verse [40]: ﴿Do you not know that God — to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ God Almighty addresses His Messenger and everyone who is fit to receive and understand from God, saying, establishing for the addressee: ﴿Do you not know that God — to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ The answer is "Yes." Therefore the judgment belongs to Him, exalted is He, and it is not disputed. Hence He punishes, and cuts off the hand of the male and female thief, and forgives whoever repents of theft and reforms. And He is over all things Competent.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of the ruling for the prescribed penalty for theft, which is cutting off the hand of the male and female thief.

2- Clarification that the thief who repents and reforms, God accepts his repentance, that is, He accepts it.

3- If the thief is not brought before the ruler, his repentance is valid even if his hand is not cut off; but if he is brought before the ruler, he has no repentance except by the amputation, and when his hand is cut off he emerges from his sin as if he had not sinned.

4- The obligation of submission to God's decree and contentment with His judgment, for He is Mighty and Wise.

Explanation of Vocabulary (Sharh al-Kalimat):

la yahzunka: al-huzn is a pain of the soul caused by fear of losing something loved.

yusari'una fi al-kufr: meaning they hasten into it, for they never left it; whenever an opportunity for disbelief arises, they display it.

qalu amanna bi-afwahihim: these are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun).

wa-min alladhina hadu: that is, the Jews.

sammaʻuna lil-kadhib: that is, those who listen to falsehood very much.

yuharrifuna al-kalim: they alter and change speech to suit their desires.

idha utitum hadha: that is, if you are given this.

fitnatahu: that is, his misguidance, due to what has already preceded in him of the causes of misguidance.

an yuṭahhira qulubahum: from disbelief and hypocrisy.

khizy: humiliation.

akkalina lil-suht: those who eat much of what is forbidden, such as bribery and usury.

aw a'ridh 'anhum: that is, do not judge between them.

bil-qist: that is, with justice.

wa-ma ula'ika bil-mu'minin: that is, not truly and in reality, even if they claim it verbally.

Explanation of the Meaning of the Verses:

The Almighty's words, ﴿O Messenger, let not those hasten to disbelief grieve you...﴾ up to ﴿...a great punishment﴾ at the end of the verse, were revealed to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to lighten what he (ﷺ) felt of inner pain from what he heard and saw from the hypocrites and the Jews. His Lord addressed him by the title of messengership, which both the hypocrites and the Jews denied: ﴿O Messenger﴾ of truth, to forbid him from the grief that multiplies his pain: ﴿let not grieve you﴾ the state of those who ﴿hasten to disbelief﴾ by denying you, for they have not left disbelief but are immersed in it. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 44–47:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Tawrah (the Torah): the Book of Musa, peace be upon him.

Huda wa nur (guidance and light): Huda (guidance) is that which leads to the goal; nur (light) is that which guides the traveler to his aim.

Hadu (those who became Jews): the Jews.

Al-Rabbaniyyun (the rabbis): plural of rabbani, the learned, wise teacher who nurtures others.

Al-Ahbar (the scholars): plural of habr, a learned person from among the People of the Book.

Wa katabna (and We prescribed): We made obligatory and required upon them.

Qisas (retaliation): equality.

Qaffayna (We caused to follow): We sent them after, with Isa son of Maryam.

Al-Fasiqun (the defiant transgressors): those who go outside obedience to Allah and His messengers.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues speaking about the Children of Israel, when the Exalted said, informing of what He gave to the Children of Israel: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light﴾, guidance from every misguidance, and a clear light for the rulings, bringing out from the darkness of ignorance. ﴿By which the prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged﴾ among the Children of Israel, ﴿the prophets who submitted﴾ to Allah with their hearts and faces, so they complied with Allah outwardly and inwardly, ﴿for those who were Jews﴾, and by it the rabbis, the people of knowledge and wisdom among the Children of Israel, judged ﴿by that which they were entrusted﴾ with, because of Allah the Exalted's entrusting them with His Book, the Torah, so they did not alter it or change anything in it, ﴿and they were witnesses over it﴾ to its truth and its freedom from deficiency and addition. Unlike you, O Jews, for you have distorted the words from their places and abandoned judging by it, so what is wrong with you? Then make manifest the truth concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the command to believe in him, and concerning the establishment of stoning for adulterers and its implementation. Do not fear people in this, but fear Allah the Exalted, for He is more worthy to be feared. And do not trade away the signs of Allah, which are His rulings, thereby suspending them, for a small price that you take from those you flatter and appease, at the expense of the religion of Allah and His Book. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - those are the disbelievers﴾. So how do you accept disbelief in place of faith?

This is what the first verse [44] indicates. As for the second verse [45], ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that a life for a life...﴾, the Exalted informed that He obligated upon the Children of Israel in the Torah retaliation for life and retribution for wounds: a soul is killed for a soul, an eye is gouged for an eye, a nose is slit for a nose, an ear is cut off for an ear, a tooth is broken for a tooth if it was broken, and extracted for a tooth if it was extracted, and wounds are answered in kind as retribution and equality. The Exalted also informed that whoever gives charity to the offender by pardoning him and not holding him accountable, that will be an expiation for his sins; and if he does not grant such charity and retaliation is carried out against him, that will be an expiation for his crime, on the condition that he presents himself for retaliation repentant, meaning regretful of his deed, seeking forgiveness from his Lord. His, the Exalted's, words at the end of the verse: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - those are the wrongdoers﴾, and that is by killing other than the killer, or killing two for one, or gouging two eyes for one eye, as the Banu Nadir used to treat the Qurayza with this, claiming nobility over them. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third [46], which is His saying: ﴿And We sent, following in their footsteps, Isa son of Maryam﴾, the Exalted informed that He sent after those earlier prophets of the Children of Israel Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, meaning He sent him directly after them, ﴿confirming that which was before him of the Torah﴾, not denying it or ignoring it, ﴿and We gave him the Injil﴾, meaning We gave him the Gospel as revelation revealed to him, and it is a holy book Allah the Exalted sent down to him, in which, that is, in the Injil, is ﴿guidance and light﴾ from misguidance and light to clarify the rulings of the lawful and unlawful. ﴿Confirming﴾, meaning the Injil confirms what came before it of the Torah, that is, affirming its rulings and establishing them, except what Allah the Exalted abrogated from it through the Injil; ﴿and guidance and instruction for the God-fearing﴾, meaning the God-fearing find in it sufficient guidance for walking their path to Allah the Exalted and complete admonition to be admonished by it in life.

This is what the third verse indicates. As for the verse [47], which is His saying: ﴿Let the People of the Injil judge by what Allah has revealed therein﴾, meaning and We said: let the People of the Injil judge; that is, We commanded the People of the Injil to judge by what Allah revealed in it of rulings, and We informed them that whoever ﴿does not judge by what Allah has revealed - those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, those who go outside His obedience. Defiance may be wrongdoing and disbelief.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The obligation of fearing Allah by performing what He made obligatory and abandoning what He forbade.

2- The disbelief of one who denies the rulings of Allah, suspending them, or plays with them by judging some and not others.

3- The obligation of retaliation for life and retribution for wounds, since what was prescribed for the Children of Israel was prescribed for this Ummah.

4- Among injustice is transgressing in retaliation, such as killing two for one, killing other than the killer, or gouging two eyes for one eye; this is disbelief when made lawful, and injustice at the same time.

5- The legitimacy of retaliation in the Injil and the obligation upon its people to apply it, and the designation of them as defiant if they suspend those rulings while believing in them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 48–50:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Kitab: the Noble Qur'an.

Min al-kitab (from the Book): a generic noun meaning the scriptures before it, such as the Tawrat (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel).

Muhayminan 'alayhi (watching over it): ruling over it, that is, verifying the truth contained in it and nullifying the falsehood that has attached itself to it.

Shir'atan wa minhajan (a law and a way): a law you act upon and a path you follow toward your happiness and perfection, from the paths of guidance.

Ummah wahidah (one community): there is no disagreement among you in belief, in worship, or in judgment.

Fastabiqu (so race to): that is, hasten to do good deeds so that those who race ahead may succeed.

An yaftinuka (that they may mislead you): that they may lead you astray from the truth.

Fa-in tawallaw (but if they turn away): they turn away from accepting the truth to which you have called them and by which you wished to judge them.

Hukm al-jahiliyyah (the judgment of ignorance): the tribal rulings practised by the people of ignorance, which are not based on the revelation of Allah the Exalted but on opinions and desires.

Meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted mentioned His sending down the Torah, that in it there is guidance and light, and mentioned the Gospel, that it too contains guidance and light, it was fitting to mention the Noble Qur'an, so He said: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿in truth﴾, bearing the truth, the truth and sincerity never departing from it, being free of addition and deletion, ﴿confirming what came before it of the Book﴾, from the earlier scriptures, and watching over them, a guardian and a judge: what is true in them is affirmed, and what is false is nullified. ﴿So judge﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿between them by what Allah has sent down﴾ to you, by killing the murderer and stoning the adulterer, not as the Jews desire, ﴿and do not follow their desires﴾ in that, and abandon the truth that has come to you. Know that We have made for every community a law and a way, that is, a specific law and path that they follow for their happiness and perfection. ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have made you one community﴾ upon one law, not differing in its matters and rulings, and He would have done so. But He diversified the laws: He made obligatory, permitted, forbade and prohibited in one law, and did not do so in another law, in order to test you in what He has given you and sent down to you, so that the obedient is distinguished from the disobedient and the guided from the astray. Therefore, come forward, ﴿so race to the good deeds﴾, that is, hasten to righteous actions, and let each one strive to be foremost, for your return is to Him, the Exalted, ﴿and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ﴾, then He will recompense you with good for good, and with evil, if He wills, likewise. This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second verse [49], Allah the Exalted in it commanded His Messenger, forbade him, warned him, informed him, and condemned his enemies. He commanded him to judge between those who come to him for judgment by what was sent down to him of the Qur'an, so He said: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has sent down﴾. He forbade him to follow the desires of the Jews, so He said: ﴿And do not follow their desires﴾. He warned him against following some of their opinions, so that he would leave some of what was sent down to him unimplemented and act upon what they proposed to him, so He said: ﴿And beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has sent down to you﴾. He informed him that if the Jews turn away, that is, turn away from accepting his judgment, which is the true and just judgment, then Allah the Exalted only intends to afflict them with a punishment as a consequence of the sins they committed and the transgressions they perpetrated, so He said: ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins﴾.

He condemned His enemies by informing that most of them are defiantly disobedient, that is, sinners who have gone outside the obedience of Allah the Exalted and His messengers, so He said: ﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient﴾. Thus He consoled him with this and eased for him what he may find of the pain of the rebellion of the Jews and the hypocrites and their turning away from the truth that he brought to them and called them to. This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third verse [50], Allah the Exalted in it denounced the Jews for seeking the judgment of the people of ignorance, where there is no revelation and no divine legislation, but only customs, desires and lusts, turning away from the judgment of the Book and the Sunnah, where justice and mercy lie. So the Exalted said: ﴿Do they then seek the judgment of ignorance?﴾ Then the Exalted informed, negating that there could be a judgment more just or more merciful than the judgment of Allah, for the people who believe with certainty in His justice and mercy, saying: ﴿And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who are certain?﴾

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to judge by the Book and the Sunnah in all matters.

2- It is not permissible to adopt any law or system other than the divine revelation, the Book and the Sunnah.

3- A warning against following the desires of people, lest one be led astray from the truth.

4- An explanation of the wisdom behind the differing laws, which is trial.

5- Most of the calamities in this world result from some sins.

6- The judgment of the Islamic law is the best of judgments in justice and mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 51–53:

Explanation of the words:

Āmanū (آمنوا): they affirmed (ṣaddaqū) Allah and His Messenger, and the promise and warning of Allah.

Awliyā' (أولياء): you show loyalty to them through support and love.

Ba'ḍuhum awliyā'u ba'ḍ (بعضهم أولياء بعض): i.e., the Jews are allies of their fellow Jews, and the Christians are allies of their fellow Christians.

Al-ẓālimīn (الظالمين): those who take as allies the enemies of Allah and His Messenger, and abandon loyalty to Allah, His Messenger and the believers.

Maraḍ (مرض): hypocrisy (nifāq), doubt (shakk) and polytheism (shirk).

Yusāri'ūna fīhim (يسارعون فيهم): i.e., hastening to persist in their loyalty, that is, loyalty to the Jews and the Christians.

Dā'ira (دائرة): that a calamity of drought turns against us, or that the affair of Islam comes to an end.

Bil-fatḥ (بالفتح): the victory of the believers over the disbelievers and the decision in their favour, such as the conquest of Makkah.

Jahda aymānihim (جهد أيمانهم): its utmost and most emphatic form.

Ḥabiṭat a'māluhum (حبطت أعمالهم): they became void and corrupt, so they gained nothing from them, because they were not for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.

The meaning of the verses:

It is related concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse that ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy each had allies among the Jews of Madinah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers were victorious at Badr, the Jews were enraged and declared their ill intentions. ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit disavowed his allies and was content with loyalty to Allah, His Messenger and the believers, but Ibn Ubayy refused this and said some of what is mentioned in these verses. So Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies﴾, i.e., for you, instead of the believers. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿They are allies of one another﴾ is a justification for the prohibition of their loyalty, for the Jew is an ally of the Jew and the Christian is an ally of the Christian against the Muslims, so how is loyalty to them permissible, and how would they be sincere in it? Is it reasonable that a Christian should love you while hating his brother, and that he would support you against his brother? His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies﴾, i.e., O believers, ﴿then indeed he is one of them﴾, because by virtue of his loyalty to them he will inevitably be a war against Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and thereby he definitely becomes one of them. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ is a causal clause indicating that whoever among the believers allies himself with the Jews and the Christians becomes like them, and so the guidance of Allah is withheld from him, because Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. Injustice (ẓulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place, and this one who allies himself with the Jews and the Christians has wronged by placing loyalty in other than its proper place, since he has opposed Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and allied himself with the Jews and the Christians, the enemies of Allah, His Messenger and the believers. This is what the first verse indicates.

As for the second verse [52], it contains some of what Ibn Ubayy said to justify his shameful position, namely continuing his loyalty to the Jews. For Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger, informing him of their condition: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, like Ibn Ubayy, and the disease is the disease of hypocrisy, ﴿they hasten into [loyalty to] them﴾, i.e., into their loyalty. He did not say "hasten toward them" because they had not left the sphere of their loyalty so as to return to it; rather they are within it, hastening, saying as those making excuses do: ﴿We fear that a misfortune may befall us﴾ from the turning of circumstances, so that we find ourselves with our allies, benefiting from them. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 54–56:

Explanation of the words:

Yartadda (من يرتد): means he returns to disbelief after his faith.

Adhillatin ʿala al-mu'minin (أذلة على المؤمنين): merciful and gentle toward them, compassionate with them.

A'izzatin ʿala al-kafirin (أعزة على الكافرين): firm and stern toward them.

Lawmata la'im (لومة لائم): the blame of one who blames.

Hizb Allah (حزب الله): the helpers of God, may He be exalted.

The meaning of the verses:

This noble verse [54], ﴿O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion...﴾, contains one of the reports of the unseen that the Qur'an conveys, and it came true exactly as it was foretold, so that it is a sign that it is the true word of God and that what was revealed to His Messenger is truly from Him. God, exalted is He, informed that whoever among the believers turns back, God, mighty and majestic, will bring a people better than them: they love God and God loves them, they are merciful toward the believers and stern toward the disbelievers, they strive in the way of God and do not fear the blame of any blamer or the reproach of any reproacher. As soon as the Messenger ﷺ died, groups of the rough Bedouin apostatized and withheld zakat, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq fought them along with the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, until they submitted to Islam and their Islam became sound. Thus Abu Bakr and his companions were among those whom God described: they love God and God loves them, they strive in His way, and they do not fear the blame of a blamer. It has been related, and it is authentically established, that when the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari was beside him, so he gestured toward him and said: "These are his people." Indeed, after the death of the Messenger, the Ash'aris came, the verse was manifested, the miracle was fulfilled, and God the Mighty has spoken the truth. As for His saying, ﴿That is the bounty of God﴾, it refers to what God granted those believers, namely Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, the Companions, and the Ash'aris, of those noble qualities: love of God, tenderness toward the believers, firmness toward the disbelievers, and striving in the way of God. As for His saying, ﴿And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, it means He is abundant in bounty and knows whom it is due to. This is what the first verse indicates.

As for the second verse [55], it contains God's reassurance to ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, and whoever disavowed the alliance with the Jews and allied himself with God and His Messenger. God informed them that He is their Protector, along with His Messenger and the believers who ﴿establish prayer and give zakat, and they bow in worship﴾, meaning they are humble and submissive. As for the alliance with the Jews and Christians, there is no good in it for them, and they are free of it. God restricted them to His alliance, the alliance of His Messenger, and the sincere believers.

In the third verse, God informed them that whoever allies himself with God, His Messenger, and the believers, God will support him and protect him from whatever concerns him, because he has become of the party of God. The party of God, that is His allies and helpers, are the victorious. This is what the noble verse indicates, which is His saying: ﴿And whoever takes God, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of God, they are the victorious.﴾

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The Noble Qur'an's report of the unseen and its truthfulness in that, making it a sign that it is the word of God.
2. The virtue of Abu Bakr, the Companions, and the Ash'aris, the people of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who are from Yemen.
3. The virtue of love of God and humility toward the believers, displaying might toward the disbelievers, the virtue of striving in the way of God, speaking the truth and steadfastness upon it, and not caring for those who blame and reproach in that.
4. The virtue of establishing prayer, giving zakat, and humility and submissiveness.
5. Alliance with God, His Messenger, and the sincere believers brings its holder victory and dominance over his enemies.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 57–60:

Explanation of the words:

*Huzuwan wa la'iban* (mockery and play): al-Huzu' is that which one is mocked at and ridiculed. Al-La'ib is that which one plays with.

*Utu al-kitab* (those given the Book): they are the Jews in this context.

*Al-kuffar* (the disbelievers): the polytheists.

*Idha nadaytum ila al-salah* (when you call to prayer): when you proclaim the adhan for it.

*Hal tanqimuna minna* (do you resent us?): that is, "do you resent us for anything?" The meaning of *tanqimuna* here is that you disapprove of us and find fault with us.

*Mathuba* (reward): recompense.

*Fasiqun* (defiantly disobedient): those who have left the obedience of God, the Exalted, through disbelief and sins.

*Al-qiradah* (the apes): the plural of *qird*, a well-known animal naturally disposed to imitation and mimicry.

*Wa al-khanazir* (and the swine): the plural of *khinzir*, a vile, well-known animal whose eating is forbidden.

*Sharr makanan* (worse in station): that is, in rank on the Day of Resurrection, in the Fire of Hell.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with a warning to the believers against taking as allies the enemies of God and His Messenger. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ in God as Lord, in Muhammad as Messenger, and in Islam as religion, ﴿do not take as allies those who have taken your religion﴾, the Islamic religion, ﴿as a mockery and play﴾: a thing they mock at, and a thing they play with, ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿and the disbelievers﴾, who are the hypocrites and the polytheists, ﴿as allies﴾ (*awliya'*): helpers, friends and confederates. ﴿And fear God, if you are believers﴾, that is, regarding taking them as allies. If you are sincere in your faith, then the love of God, His Messenger and the believers cannot coexist with the love of the enemies of God, His Messenger and the believers. This is what the first verse [57] indicates.

As for the second verse [58], it contains God's information that confirms the obligation to oppose those who take the religion of the believers as a mockery and play. These are the ones who, when they hear the adhan calling to prayer, take it as a mockery and play. One of them says, "What is this sound?" and another says, "This is the bray of a donkey." May God disfigure their speech and humiliate them. God, the Exalted, said about them: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and play. That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾ Indeed, they do not reason; for if they reasoned, the call to prayer would be among the sweetest things that rational people hear, because it is a call to purity and purification, to goodness, love and harmony, a call to the remembrance and worship of God. But these people, as God, the Exalted, has told us about them, ﴿do not reason﴾; their condition is that of beasts, and beasts are better than them. This is what the second verse indicates.

As for the third verse [59], it contains God's instruction to His Messenger to say to those Jews and the wicked disbelievers: "O People of the Book, you resent us in your hostility toward us and your fighting against us, [but] what do you resent from us? Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 61–63:

Explanation of the words:

Yaktumun (they conceal): that is, they hide and suppress in their souls what is within them.

Fi al-ithm wa al-'udwan (in sin and transgression): al-ithm (sin) is everything harmful and corrupt, namely what Allah the Exalted has forbidden, whether in belief, speech or action; al-'udwan (transgression) is injustice.

As-suht (unlawful gain): unlawful wealth such as bribery (rishwa) and usury (riba), and whatever they take in money in exchange for distorting the words and misinterpreting them.

Ar-rabbaniyyun and al-ahbar: ar-rabbaniyyun here are the devoted worshippers who educate others, like the shaykhs of Sufism among us. Al-ahbar are the scholars.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in exposing and clarifying their corruption, to increase the aversion to allying with them. Allah the Exalted informs in the first verse about their hypocrites, saying: ﴿When they come to you, they say, "We believe,"﴾ meaning: they mingle with you in your gatherings. ﴿But they had entered with disbelief and they had certainly left with it.﴾ They did not believe, but were hypocrites and nothing else; they entered with disbelief in their hearts and left with it. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing﴾ of disbelief and plotting against you. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted in the first verse [61]: ﴿When they come to you, they say, "We believe," but they had entered with disbelief and they had certainly left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they were concealing.﴾

As for the second verse [62], Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger that, because of the abundance of sins they commit and the evils they engage in, you see many of them hastening toward sin and transgression, and consuming unlawful gain openly, not concealing it or hiding it. Then Allah the Exalted condemned them for that and denounced their deed, saying: ﴿Wretched is what they were doing.﴾

In the last verse, He rebuked their worshippers and scholars for their silence about the crimes of their common folk and their approval of them, out of flattery and appeasement. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Why do the rabbaniyyun and the rabbis not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of unlawful gain?﴾ meaning: why do they not forbid them from their sinful speech, that is lying, and from their consumption of unlawful gain, that is bribery and usury? Then Allah the Exalted condemned the scholars' silence about them, saying: ﴿Wretched is what they were producing﴾, meaning: by My might and My majesty, wretched is the work of these people, in that deliberate silence for the sake of particular benefits they obtain has become a craft they have perfected and mastered. And we seek refuge in Allah.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The presence of hypocrites among the Jews in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ) in Madinah.

2- Clarification of the recklessness of the Jews and their indifference to committing crimes openly.

3- The ugliness of scholars' silence over wrongdoing and their turning a blind eye to its perpetrators; for this reason, many of the early scholars said that this verse is the most severe and most dangerous verse for scholars.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Yad Allah maghlulah* (the hand of God is chained): they mean that God has restricted their provision and not widened it for them.

*Ghullat aydihim* (their hands are chained): a supplication against them, that they be deprived of spending in good and in what benefits them.

*La'anu bima qalu* (they were cursed for what they said): they were expelled from God's mercy because of their describing the Lord, exalted is He, with stinginess.

*Bal yadahu mabsutatan* (rather, both His hands are outstretched): not as they said, may God curse them: "The hand of God is chained," meaning withholding from spending.

*Tughyanan* (transgression): exceeding the limit of moderation in their false saying and their corrupt deeds.

*Wa alqayna baynahum* (And We cast among them): that is, among the Jews and the Christians.

*Awqadu naran* (they kindled a fire): that is, the fire of strife, incitement, instigation and enmities for war.

*Wa law anna ahl al-kitab* (And if the People of the Book): the Jews and the Christians.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 67–69:

Explanation of the words:

al-Rasul (the Messenger): one of the children of Adam to whom a law was revealed and who was commanded to convey it; here it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Balligh ma unzila ilayka (convey what has been sent down to you): of the Tawhid (the Oneness of God), the laws (shara'i') and the rulings (ahkam).

Ya'simuka (will protect you): will guard you with a guarding such that no one can reach you with harm.

Fala ta'as (do not grieve): do not be sorrowful and do not be sad.

Hadu (those who were Jews): the Jews.

al-Sabi'un (the Sabians): plural of sabi'; they are a sect among the People of the Book.

Meaning of the verses:

In the first verse [67], the Lord, blessed and exalted, addresses His Messenger, honouring him by saying: ﴿O Messenger﴾, in order to command him to convey what was revealed to him of beliefs, laws and rulings, so He says: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. And He says to him: ﴿And if you do not do so﴾, meaning, if you fall short in conveying anything for any reason whatsoever, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, meaning, it is as if you had conveyed nothing. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾, meaning, He will prevent them from touching you with any harm. Therefore you have no excuse for leaving off conveying anything, whether it relates to the People of the Book or to others. Thus the Messenger of Allah never concealed anything of what he was commanded to convey, not at all. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, it confirms His promise to protect His Messenger (ﷺ), since He, exalted is He, does not grant success to the disbelievers in what they wish and desire of harming His Messenger (ﷺ). When this verse was revealed, he (ﷺ) said: "Do not guard me, for Allah has protected me." This is what the first verse indicates. As for the second [68], which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾, this context has already preceded and is repeated here as confirmation and emphasis. It is an announcement from Allah, exalted is He, that the Jews and the Christians are not upon any part of the true religion, nor under the guardianship of Allah, exalted is He, until they establish what they were commanded, what they were forbidden, and what they were called to of good deeds and righteous actions, which came in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an as well. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾, this is an informing from Allah, exalted is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ) that what Allah reveals to His Messenger and sends down to him in His Book, concerning the reports about the People of the Book which clarify their sins and their misguidance, and what is a command to them to believe in the unlettered Prophet and to follow him in the true religion with which he was sent, increases many of them in transgression, meaning haughtiness and insolence, and disbelief over and above their disbelief. Therefore, "do not grieve" means do not be sorrowful over their not believing in you and in what you have brought, for they are a disbelieving people. As for the third verse [69], which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians﴾, then "those who believed" are the Muslims; the Jews, the Christians and the Sabians, who are a sect among them, are the People of the Book. So whoever among all these groups believes the true belief in Allah and the Last Day and brings what necessarily accompanies faith, which is piety, meaning abstaining from polytheism and sins, in deeds and in abstentions, then "there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve," neither in this world, nor in the barzakh, nor on the Day of Resurrection, and no grief will reach them in the three lives. Allah's promise is true, and who is more truthful in statement than Allah!

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of conveying on the Messengers, and our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) rising to this duty in its most perfect and complete form.

2- The absolute infallibility (ismah) of the Messenger.

3- The disbelief of the People of the Book, except those among them who believe in the Prophet (ﷺ) and follow what he brought of the true religion.

4- Those who are obstinate and arrogant are not increased by proofs and evidences except in insolence, aversion, transgression and disbelief.

5- What counts is faith, righteous deeds, and abstaining from polytheism and sins, not affiliation to any religion.

As for the second [68], which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Book, you are not upon anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾, this context has already preceded and is repeated here as confirmation and emphasis. It is an announcement from Allah, exalted is He, that the Jews and the Christians are not upon any part of the true religion, nor under the guardianship of Allah, exalted is He, until they establish what they were commanded, what they were forbidden, and what they were called to of good deeds and righteous actions, which came in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an as well. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And what has been sent down to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾, this is an informing from Allah, exalted is He, to His Messenger (ﷺ) that what Allah reveals to His Messenger and sends down to him in His Book, concerning the reports about the People of the Book which clarify their sins and their misguidance, and what is a command to them to believe in the unlettered Prophet and to follow him in the true religion with which he was sent, increases many of them in transgression, meaning haughtiness and insolence, and disbelief over and above their disbelief. Therefore, "do not grieve" means do not be sorrowful over their not believing in you and in what you have brought, for they are a disbelieving people. As for the third verse [69], which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians﴾, then "those who believed" are the Muslims; the Jews, the Christians and the Sabians, who are a sect among them, are the People of the Book. So whoever among all these groups believes the true belief in Allah and the Last Day and brings what necessarily accompanies faith, which is piety, meaning abstaining from polytheism and sins, in deeds and in abstentions, then "there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve," neither in this world, nor in the barzakh, nor on the Day of Resurrection, and no grief will reach them in the three lives. Allah's promise is true, and who is more truthful in statement than Allah!

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation of conveying on the Messengers, and our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) rising to this duty in its most perfect and complete form.

2- The absolute infallibility (ismah) of the Messenger.

3- The disbelief of the People of the Book, except those among them who believe in the Prophet (ﷺ) and follow what he brought of the true religion.

4- Those who are obstinate and arrogant are not increased by proofs and evidences except in insolence, aversion, transgression and disbelief.

5- What counts is faith, righteous deeds, and abstaining from polytheism and sins, not affiliation to any religion.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 70–72:

Explanation of the words:

al-Mithaq (the covenant): a pledge affirmed by oath.

Bima la tahwa anfusuhum (with what their souls do not desire): with what they do not love and what their diseased souls do not incline toward.

Fariqan kadhdhabu (a group they denied): that is, they denied one group of the messengers and killed another group.

An la takuna fitnah (that they would not be afflicted): that is, that they would not be tested for their sins with hardships and trials.

Fa'amu wa sammu (they became blind and deaf): they were blind to the lessons and deaf to the hearing of admonitions.

Man yushrik billah (whoever associates partners with God): that is, he associates with God another being from among all created things, worshipping it alongside God in any kind of worship.

Harram Allahu 'alayhi al-jannah (God has forbidden him Paradise): He has decreed that he be barred from entering it forever, unless he repents of associating partners.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues speaking about the People of the Book. God swore that He took the covenant of the Children of Israel, which is in the Torah, that they would worship God alone in accordance with what He prescribed for them, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions. He sent to them His messengers in succession; whenever a messenger came to them with what did not agree with their desires, they denied him in what he brought and called them to, or they killed him. They thought they would not be held accountable for their sins, so they became blind to the truth and deaf to the hearing of admonitions. Their Lord then tested them and let loose upon them those who inflicted on them the evil of punishment. Then God turned to them in forgiveness, they repented, their affairs were set right and their conditions became good. Then they became blind and deaf again, except for a few among them, so He let loose upon them those who inflicted on them the evil of punishment as well. And here they are, in blindness and deafness, and God is Seeing of what they do, and He will surely bring down His punishment upon them if they do not repent, believe in God and His Messenger, and adopt the true religion, which is Islam.

This is what the first and second verses [70–71] contain. As for the third verse [72], which is His saying: ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, God is the Messiah, the son of Mary"﴾, God, affirming His ruling of disbelief upon those who slander Him and His Messenger, informs that they claim that God, exalted is His majesty and great is His authority, is the Messiah son of Mary — exalted is God far above having a servant among His servants. Far be it from Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger, that he would accept being told, "You are God." And how could he, when he is the one who said: ﴿O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates partners with God — God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire, and there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers﴾. So would such a statement come from one who claims that he is God or the son of God? Glory be to You, O God, this is a tremendous slander.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- An account of the history of the Children of Israel, and the revealing of the hidden crimes they committed, including disbelief and killing.

2- God's honoring of the Children of Israel and His kindness toward them despite their rebellion against Him, their rejection of His covenant, their killing of His prophets, their denial, and the deceit they practised.

3- Affirmation of the disbelief of the Christians in their saying that the Messiah is God.

4- Affirmation of the servitude of Jesus, peace be upon him, to his Lord, exalted is He.

5- The forbidding of Paradise to whoever meets his Lord while associating anything with Him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 73–76:

Explanation of the words:

*Thalithu thalatha* (ثالث ثلاثة, "the third of three"): the three are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, all of whom they consider to be one God.

*Khalat min qablihi al-rusul* (خلت من قبله الرسل, "messengers passed before him"): many messengers had gone before him.

*Wa ummuhu siddiqah* (وأمه صديقة, "and his mother was a truthful woman"): i.e., Maryam was greatly truthful in her speech and her deeds.

*Anna yu'fakun* (أنى يؤفكون, "how are they turned away"): i.e., how are they diverted from the truth when it has become clear and manifest?

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues to explain the disbelief of the Christians. In the previous passage, the disbelief of those who said that God is the Messiah son of Maryam was mentioned; in this passage, the disbelief of those who said that God is the third of three is mentioned. God, exalted is He, said in this verse [73]: "Indeed, those who say, 'God is the third of three,' have disbelieved." They mean the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; some of them say the Father, the Son, and the Mother, and the three are one God. God refuted them in their saying and rejected their falsehood, saying: "There is no god except one God." That is, the matter is not as they lie about; rather, God is one God. As for Gabriel, he is one of His angels; Jesus is His servant and messenger; and Maryam is His handmaiden. All of them are servants of God alone, besides whom there is no god and no lord.

Then God, exalted is He, threatened these disbelieving liars: "And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will certainly afflict those of them who disbelieve." He swore by Himself that if they do not desist from their false saying, which is disbelief, a painful punishment, extremely distressing, will afflict them.

Then, out of the perfection of His mercy, mighty and majestic is He, in the second verse [74] He called them to repentance so that He might turn to them and forgive them, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. He, mighty and majestic, said: "Will they not turn in repentance to God?" By abandoning this disbelief and falsehood, and seek God's forgiveness for it. God is Forgiving toward those who repent and Merciful toward the believers.

In the third verse [75], God, exalted is He, informed and taught His Messenger the argument against the falsehood of the Christians, saying: "The Messiah, son of Maryam, was only a messenger." So he was neither a lord nor a god; rather, he was an honored messenger, and many honored messengers had passed before him. His mother Maryam was also not a god, as they claim; she was a woman from the women of the Children of Israel, a truthful woman, greatly truthful throughout her life, who knew neither lying nor falsehood. She and her son Jesus, peace be upon them both, were two human beings like all other humans. This is shown by the fact that they both ate food, needing it, because their bodies could not subsist without it. Would one who eats food out of need for it, and then excretes its waste, be fit to be a god? Certainly not.

Here He said to His Messenger ﷺ: "Look, O our Messenger, how We make the signs clear to them, which plainly show the falsehood of their disbelief. Then look how they are turned away from the truth," that is, how they are diverted from it, though it is clear and manifest.

In the final verse [76], He commanded His Messenger to say to those who have been turned away from the truth and diverted from its proofs, who do not reflect upon them, rebuking them: "Do you worship besides God that which possesses neither harm nor benefit for you?" This refers to Jesus and his mother, while you abandon the worship of Him who possesses that power, namely God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The refutation of the Trinity in the Christian creed and the affirmation of monotheism.

2- The clearing of Jesus and his mother, peace be upon them, from the claim of divinity for people.

3- The opening of the door of repentance to the Christians, should they repent.

4- The affirmation of the humanity of Jesus and Maryam, peace be upon them, by the evidence of their need for food to sustain their bodies; and whoever is in need cannot validly be a god, by reason and by law.

5- The condemnation of everyone who worships other than God, since all creatures are in need, possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves or for their worshippers, do not hear the prayers of those who call upon them, and know nothing of their state. God alone is the All-Hearing of the sayings of all His servants, the All-Knowing of all their conditions and deeds; He alone is the one truly worthy of worship, and whatever else is worshipped is false.

His mother Maryam was also not a god, as they claim; she was a woman from the women of the Children of Israel, a truthful woman, greatly truthful throughout her life, who knew neither lying nor falsehood. She and her son Jesus, peace be upon them both, were two human beings like all other humans. This is shown by the fact that they both ate food, needing it, because their bodies could not subsist without it. Here He said to His Messenger ﷺ: "Look, O our Messenger, how We make the signs clear to them, which plainly show the falsehood of their disbelief. Then look how they are turned away from the truth," that is, how they are diverted from it, though it is clear and manifest.

1- The refutation of the Trinity in the Christian creed and the affirmation of monotheism.

2- The clearing of Jesus and his mother, peace be upon them, from the claim of divinity for people.

3- The opening of the door of repentance to the Christians, should they repent.

4- The affirmation of the humanity of Jesus and Maryam, peace be upon them, by the evidence of their need for food to sustain their bodies; and whoever is in need cannot validly be a god, by reason and by law.

5- The condemnation of everyone who worships other than God, since all creatures are in need, possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves or for their worshippers, do not hear the prayers of those who call upon them, and know nothing of their state. God alone is the All-Hearing of the sayings of all His servants, the All-Knowing of all their conditions and deeds; He alone is the one truly worthy of worship, and whatever else is worshipped is false.

Meaning of the Verses:

The discourse continues concerning the People of the Book, Jews and Christians. Allah, the Exalted, said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O our Messenger: ﴿O People of the Book﴾, and here it refers to the Christians: ﴿Do not exceed the limits in your religion, beyond the truth﴾, that is, do not be excessively strict in what is not the truth which Allah has prescribed for you, so that you invent innovations and go to extremes in adhering to them and defending them. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of Dāwūd﴾. Some of them were transformed into apes, ﴿and ʿĪsā son of Maryam﴾, as some of them were transformed into swine, and they were cursed upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ) in more than one verse of the Noble Qur'an. This curse, which is distance from all good and mercy and what necessitates it in this world and the Hereafter, has as its cause what Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in His saying: ﴿That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing﴾.

That is, because of their disobedience to Allah and His messengers by abandoning obligations and committing prohibitions, and their transgression in religion through exaggeration and innovation, and by killing the prophets and righteous among them. Allah, the Exalted, informed in the third verse of the type of their disobedience and transgression for which they were cursed, saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from any evil they committed﴾, that is, when they had become deserving of the curse, they would commit a great evil and none of them would forbid another, as the Prophet (ﷺ) informed in his saying: «Indeed, the first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another and say: "O such-and-such, fear Allah and leave what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you." Then He said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿You see many of them﴾, that is, of the Jews in Medina, ﴿taking as allies those who disbelieve﴾, meaning the polytheists and hypocrites in Mecca and Medina, accompanying them, showing affection to them and supporting them, while knowing that they are disbelievers whose allegiance is forbidden in their religion and their scripture. Then Allah, the Exalted, condemned their deed, saying: ﴿Evil is what their own souls have sent forward for them﴾, as a result of the evil, disbelief and corruption to which these things led them, which is the wrath of Allah upon them and their eternal abiding in punishment from their death onward without any end. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Evil is what their souls have sent forward for them: that Allah is wrathful toward them, and in punishment they will abide forever﴾, never leaving it.

Then Allah, the Exalted, further affirmed their disbelief, falsehood, evil and corruption, saying: ﴿And if they had believed in Allah﴾ as belief in Him is obligatory, and in the Prophet Muhammad and in what he brought of guidance and the religion of truth, and what was revealed to him of the Qur'an and the clear signs, they would not have taken the disbelieving polytheists and hypocrites as allies. But the cause of this is that they are defiantly disobedient, except a few of them, and the one who is defiant of Allah's command and outside His obedience does not stop at any limit in corruption, ever. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if they had believed in Allah, and the Prophet, and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾.

Lessons from the Verses:

1- The prohibition of exaggeration and innovation in religion, and of following the people of desires.

2- Disobedience and transgression bring their possessor deprivation and loss.

3- The prohibition of remaining silent about evil, and the gravity of its consequence upon society.

4- The prohibition of allegiance to the people of disbelief, evil and corruption.

5- Allegiance to the people of disbelief through affection and support, to the exclusion of the believers, is a sign of disbelief and its mark in its possessor.

We were commanded to honor the Messenger (ﷺ); calling upon him is ghuluw in religion.

The desires of a people who have already gone astray (ahwā'a qawmin qad ḍallū): plural of hawā (desire). The possessor of desire is one who believes, says, and acts according to what he desires, not according to what has been established by proof and confirmed by evidence from the religion of Allah, the Exalted.

And they led many astray (wa aḍallū kathīran): that is, they led a great number of people astray by their desires and falsehoods.

From the even path (ʿan sawā' al-sabīl): sawā' al-sabīl means the middle of the road, the just path, with no deviation to the right or to the left.
