Explanation of the meanings of the words:

**ʿAdawah** (enmity): an inner hatred that keeps its bearer far from the one he opposes, so that he does not reach him with good nor draw near to him in affection, and it may lead him to desire evil for the enemy.

**Mawaddah** (affection): an inner love that makes its bearer draw near to the one he loves, seeking to do him good and ward off harm.

**Qassisin** (priests): plural of qassis, the religious head among the Christians, so called for his knowledge.

**Wa-rahbanan** (monks): the rahban are plural of rahib, from rahbah (awe). He is a man among the Christians who devotes himself to worship and withdraws to a monastery (dayr) or a hermitage (sawmaʿah).

**Ma unzila ila rasul** (what was revealed to the Messenger): the Messenger is Muhammad (ﷺ), and what was revealed to him is the verses of the Noble Qur'an that show the honour of ʿIsa and his mother Maryam (peace be upon them), and that ʿIsa is a servant of Allah.

**Al-shahidin** (the witnesses): plural of shahid, those who bear witness to Allah's oneness and to the Prophet Muhammad's prophethood, and remain steadfast in that.

**Al-salihin** (the righteous): plural of salih, one who fulfils the rights of Allah completely, by faith in Him and by thanking Him for His blessings through obedience, and who fulfils the rights of people completely, by doing good to them and restraining harm from them.

**Fa-athabahum Allah bi-ma qalu** (Allah rewarded them for what they said): He recompensed them, for their words of faith and for the deeds they were enabled to perform, with gardens beneath which rivers flow.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah informs His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) of the enmity of both the Jews and the polytheists towards the believers, and that they are fiercer in enmity than others. He says: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah.﴾ As for the Jews, it is because they inherited from generation to generation the denial of truth and the standing against its callers, in addition to their hope of restoring their former glory and state, which conflicts with the Islamic call. As for the polytheists, it is due to their ignorance, their excess in forbidden things, and the superstitions, polytheism and misguidance they became accustomed to through long ages.

Allah also informs that the Christians are the nearest in affection to those who believe, saying: ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians."﴾ He explains this nearness in affection by His saying: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾ That is, this was due to the fact that among them are priests and monks. The priests are scholars of the Scripture and generally religious leaders who prefer justice, mercy and goodness over oppression, cruelty and evil. The monks, because they detach themselves from the world and have no desire for it. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿and because they are not arrogant﴾ towards the truth, accepting it and speaking by it. Therefore, when materialism pervaded Christian societies and atheism and licentiousness spread among them, that affection for the believers diminished, if it did not cease altogether.

As for His saying: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they recognise of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ It refers to those Christians who embraced Islam as soon as the Qur'an was recited to them and they heard it, such as Ashamah al-Najashi and a large group. The meaning of their words ﴿so register us among the witnesses﴾ is that, after hearing the Qur'an, they were moved by it, wept because of what they recognised of the truth, and asked Allah to register them among the witnesses, so that they would be with them in Paradise. The witnesses are those who bore witness to Allah's oneness and to His Messenger's prophethood, and obeyed Allah and His Messenger from this Ummah. Their words: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, and aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people?﴾ mean: what prevents us from believing in Allah as Lord and one God, having no partner, no child and no parent?

[They also say] by what has come of the truth regarding His oneness and the prophethood of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in hope that our Lord will admit us to Paradise with the righteous of this Ummah. When they said this, Allah informed them that He rewarded them for it: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Allah also informs that this recompense He gave them is ﴿the reward of the doers of good﴾, those who did good in word and deed together with soundness of belief and purity of soul, not having been stained by polytheism or sins. Then Allah informs that those who disbelieved in Allah as one God and in His Messenger as prophet and messenger, and denied His Qur'anic verses, those distant ones are the companions of the Blazing Fire, in which they will abide forever.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The gravity of the enmity of the Jews and polytheists toward Islam and the Muslims.
2. The nearness of sincere Christians in their Christianity to the Muslims.
3. The virtue of humility and the ugliness of arrogance.
4. The excellence and honour of this Ummah over the nations before it.
5. The virtue of the People of the Book when they embrace Islam, and the goodness of their Islam.
6. Explanation of the fate of the disbelievers and deniers, which is their abiding forever in the Fire of Hell.
7. The Qur'an's method of encouragement and warning, mentioning the threat after the promise.

**Qassisin** (priests): plural of qassis, the religious head among the Christians, so called for his knowledge.

**Wa-rahbanan** (monks): the rahban are plural of rahib, from rahbah (awe). He is a man among the Christians who devotes himself to worship and withdraws to a monastery (dayr) or a hermitage (sawmaʿah).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 87–89:

Explanation of the words:

*Lā tuḥarrimū* (do not forbid): *al-taḥrīm* means prohibition; i.e., do not refrain (from them).

*Mā aḥalla Allāh lakum* (what God has made lawful for you): i.e., what He has permitted you and allowed you to enjoy, such as marriage, food, and drink.

*Ḥalālan ṭayyiban* (lawful and good): permissible, not repugnant nor disgusting.

*Lā yu'ākhidhukum Allāh bil-laghw* (God will not hold you accountable for idle oaths): God will not punish you for the *laghw* (idle oath), which is that which was not made with the intention of swearing.

*'Aqqadtum al-aymān* (you have bound the oaths): you resolved upon them in your hearts, to do or not to do something.

*Min awsaṭi* (of the middle [standard]): the bulk of it, neither the best of it nor the worst of it.

*Ahlīkum* (your families): wives and children.

*Taḥrīr raqaba* (freeing a slave): freeing the neck from the bondage that holds it.

*Yubayyinu Allāh lakum āyātihi* (God makes clear to you His signs): those that contain the rulings of His religion, of obligation, lawfulness, and prohibition.

Meaning of the verses:

Verses 87 and 88 were revealed concerning some of the Companions, among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn and others. They had attended an exhortation that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave them, so they became detached from the world and desirous of the Hereafter. They resolved to practice celibacy and withdrawal from the world. They came to the Mother of the Believers ʿĀ'isha (may God be pleased with her) and asked her about the prayer and night worship of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), as if they regarded it as too little. One of them said: "I will not approach women." Another said: "I will fast and never break my fast, all my life." Another said: "I will stand in prayer and never sleep." When this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he addressed the people and said: "What is wrong with people who say such and such? I eat meat, I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you﴾, of food, drink, and women, ﴿and do not transgress﴾ by going beyond what is lawful for you to what is forbidden for you, for God, your Lord, ﴿does not love the transgressors﴾. ﴿And eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good﴾. As for the unlawful, it is not a provision for you. ﴿And fear God﴾, i.e., fear Him by abandoning excess and extremism that leads you to asceticism, for there is no monasticism in Islam. ﴿In whom you believe﴾, i.e., a Lord who legislates, makes lawful and unlawful, and a God who is obeyed and worshipped. This is what the first and second verses indicate.

As for the third verse, God's saying ﴿God will not hold you accountable for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾, it was revealed when that group of the Messenger of God's Companions said (We have sworn to what we resolved upon of celibacy, so what shall we do with our oaths?). God then made clear to them what is required of them in their oaths when they broke them by deviating from what they had sworn to. He said: ﴿God will not hold you accountable for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾, which is an oath in which there was no intention to swear, but the wording of the oath merely passed over the tongue, such as "No, by God" or "Yes, by God." Similar to this is swearing about a matter one believes to be a certain way, only for it to turn out otherwise than one thought. ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths﴾, i.e., what you intended and resolved upon. So whoever breaks an oath after swearing, the obligation upon him, to be free from sin, is an expiation (*kaffāra*), which is ﴿feeding ten needy persons﴾, for each needy person half a *ṣā'* (i.e., two *mudds*) of the middle standard ﴿of what you feed your families﴾, neither of the best and costliest, nor of the worst and cheapest. ﴿Or clothing them﴾, such as a shirt and a turban, or a wrapper and a cloak. ﴿Or freeing a slave﴾, i.e., freeing a believing slave, whether male or female, young or old. Of these three the believer has the choice to expiate by whichever he wishes. If he does not find (the means), then ﴿fasting for three days﴾, consecutively or separately, as he wishes. This is the meaning of God's saying ﴿whoever does not find (the means), then fasting three days﴾. And His saying ﴿that is the expiation of your oaths﴾, i.e., this which has been explained to you is what you expiate with for the sin of breaking the oath that has attached itself to your souls.

And His saying ﴿and guard your oaths﴾, i.e., do not multiply oaths, lest you break them and thus sin, and so expiation becomes obligatory upon you for that. And God's saying: ﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may be grateful﴾ means: like this clarification which He has made to you regarding the matter of breaking oaths and their expiation, He makes clear to you His signs, which contain His laws and the markers of His religion, in order to prepare you thereby to thank Him by obedience, by doing what He commands you and abstaining from what He forbids. So to Him belong all praise and favor.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The prohibition of forbidding what God has permitted, just as it is prohibited to make lawful what God, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden.

2- Clarification of the extent of the Companions' eagerness to obey God, out of fear of His punishment and hope for His bounty.

3- The prohibition of excess in religion and extremism in it.

4- Detailed explanation of the expiation for oaths.

5- Disliking the frequent swearing of oaths, and the absolute prohibition of swearing by other than God, the Exalted.

6- Recommendation to break an oath to abandon a recommended act or do a disliked act, and to expiate for it. As for one who swears to abandon an obligation or to commit a prohibited act, breaking such an oath is obligatory, and expiation is required.

7- Oaths are of three kinds: *laghw* (idle): an oath for which there is no expiation, since there is no sin in it. *Ghamūs* (perjurious): swearing while deliberately lying, for which there is no expiation except repentance. *Mukaffara* (expiable oath): the oath in which the believer intentionally and purposefully swears, to do or not to do something, and then breaks it; this is the kind whose expiation God mentioned and explained.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 90–93:

Explanation of the words:

Al-khamr (intoxicants) and al-maysir (gambling): khamr is every intoxicant, whatever its substance, whether little or much; maysir is gambling (qimar).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 94–96:

Explanation of the words:

Yablunnakum (ليبلونكم): He will test you.

As-sayd (الصيد): That which is hunted.

Tanaluhu aydikum (تناله أيديكم): such as birds' eggs and their chicks.

Wa rimahukum (ورماحكم): plural of rumh (spear); what is reached by them is animals of various kinds.

Li-ya'lama Allahu man yakhafuhu bil-ghayb (ليعلم الله من يخافه بالغيب): That God Most High, through this test, may make manifest who fears Him in the unseen and so does not hunt.

Fa-man i'tada (بعد التحريم) (fa-man i'tada (after the prohibition)): meaning, one who hunts after the prohibition has reached him.

Wa antum hurum (وأنتم حرم): plural of haram (one in a state of ihram); haram refers to one in ihram for hajj or 'umrah, and one says rajul haram and imra'ah haram.

Min al-ni'am (من النعم): al-ni'am: camels, cattle and sheep.

Dhawa 'adlin minkum (ذوا عدل منكم): that is, two just persons of knowledge.

Wabal amrih (وبال أمره): the heaviness of the recompense for his sin, since he hunted while hunting was forbidden.

Wa-lis-sayyarah (وللسيارة): the travellers who take provision from it on their journey. The food of the sea is what the sea casts up onto the shore.

Meaning of the verses:

The Lord, blessed and exalted, addresses His believing servants to inform them, emphasising His report, that He will test them so that the obedient may be distinguished from the disobedient. He said: ﴿O you who believe, Allah will surely test you with something of game that your hands and your spears can reach, so that Allah may make evident who fears Him in the unseen﴾. Thus He forbade them hunting while they were in the state of ihram, then tested them by placing it before them, within easy reach of their hands and spears, with complete ease, in the manner in which the Children of Israel were tested with the prohibition of hunting on the Sabbath: fish came to them on their Sabbath openly, and on the days when they did not keep the Sabbath it did not come to them. Thus their Lord tested them because they were defiant. However, the Muslims responded to their Lord and complied with His command, unlike the Children of Israel, who disobeyed and hunted, so He transformed them into apes, despised. And His saying, ﴿So whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment﴾, means: whoever hunts after this prohibition will have a painful punishment. This is what the first verse [94] indicates.

As for the second verse [95], which is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾, it emphasises for them the prohibition of hunting and explains to them the recompense that follows from it. He said: ﴿And whoever of you kills it intentionally﴾, so the obligatory ruling upon the one who kills it is recompense ﴿equivalent to what he killed of livestock﴾, namely camels, cattle and sheep. ﴿Two just persons from among you shall judge concerning it﴾. The two just persons look at the game and what resembles it among the livestock: the ostrich resembles the camel, the wild cow resembles the cow, and the gazelle resembles the ram, and so on. Then whoever is obliged to give a camel, a cow, or a ram may, if he wishes, bring it as an offering to the poor of the Haram at Makkah, and if he wishes he may buy food with its value and give it in charity, and if he wishes he may fast, one day for every half sa' [of food]. This is based on His saying: ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or as expiation: feeding the poor, or the equivalent of that in fasting﴾. And His saying: ﴿that he may taste the heaviness of his deed﴾, meaning the heaviness of the recompense for his disobedience. And His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past﴾, meaning He has ceased to hold you accountable for what has passed. As for the future, He says: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him, and Allah is Mighty, Able to exact retribution﴾, meaning He will punish him for his disobedience, and nothing prevents His will. ﴿Beware of Allah, and beware of hunting while you are in the state of ihram.﴾ This is what the second verse indicates. As for the third [96], Allah Most High, after prohibiting hunting to the believers while they are in ihram and mandating recompense for the one who hunts, has informed them.

He informed that, as a favour from Him to them, He has made lawful to them the game of the sea, that is, what they catch from the sea while in ihram, just as He made its food lawful to them, which is the dead creatures the sea casts onto its shore. ﴿A provision for you and for the travellers﴾, who take provision from it on their journey. Hunting on land is forbidden to them as long as they are in ihram. He commanded them to fear Him, that is, to fear His punishment, so that they would adhere to obedience to Him by performing what He made obligatory and abstaining from what He forbade. He also reminded them that they will all be gathered to Him on the Day of Resurrection for reckoning and recompense, saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered.﴾

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- God Most High tested the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyyah with an abundance of game before them. He forbade them to hunt it, and they obeyed God's command and did not hunt, so they were better than the Children of Israel and more excellent than them in the time of their prophets.

2- The prohibition of hunting for the one in ihram, except the game of the sea, which is permitted to him.

3- Explanation of the recompense for one who hunts while in ihram, and that it is the recompense equivalent to what he killed of livestock.

4- The obligation of arbitration regarding what the one in ihram has hunted, and it is not valid for the hunter to expiate by himself.

5- The game of the Haram is forbidden to those in ihram among people, and to those not in ihram.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 97–100:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Ka'bah: Every square building is called a ka'bah, and what is meant here is the Sacred House of Allah.

Qiyaman lin-nas (a means of standing/establishment for mankind): Through it their religious affairs are sustained, by the pilgrimage (hajj) to it and the lesser pilgrimage ('umrah), and their worldly affairs are sustained by the security within it and the gathering of the fruits of everything to it.

Ash-shahr al-haram (the sacred month): That is, the forbidden month. What is meant is the four sacred months: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram.

Al-hady (the offerings): What is brought as gifts to the House of the various kinds of offerings.

Wal-qala'id (the garlands): Plural of qaladah, which is what is hung on a camel or cow offered to the Sacred Precinct.

Al-balagh (the conveying): The conveying of what he was commanded to convey.

Ma tubduna wa ma taktumun (what you show and what you conceal): That is, what you make apparent and what you hide.

Al-khabith (the corrupt): The opposite of the good (at-tayyib); it means the forbidden, and it is general in both perceptible and intelligible things.

Ulu al-albab (people of understanding): The people of intellect.

The meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of standing for mankind﴾: What is meant by "mankind" is the Arabs in their pre-Islamic ignorance. The meaning of "qiyaman" is that their interests stand upon the existence of the House, to which people come for hajj and 'umrah, and in which whoever enters its sanctuary is secure. Likewise the sacred month, which are four months: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram and Rajab. Likewise the offerings, which are the livestock brought to the Sanctuary, and likewise the garlands, the plural of qaladah, which is what is hung on the offering to show that it is brought to the Sanctuary, and likewise what is hung on the one who goes to the Sanctuary himself, from the bark of the trees of the Sanctuary, to announce that he comes from the Sanctuary or goes to it. These four—the Sacred House, the sacred month, the offerings and the garlands—were standing in place of authority among the Arabs, so security and prosperity were realized in their lands, especially for the people of the Sanctuary from the tribe of Quraysh. This is from the arrangement of Allah, may He be exalted, for His servants, and it indicates His knowledge, power, wisdom and mercy. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. That is, He realized that security and prosperity at a time when you had no state and no order, so that He might make you know that He knows what is in the heavens and the earth of all creatures and the various kinds of created beings, nothing of their affairs being hidden from Him, and that He is Knowing of all things. He is the true God, there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him, so worship Him, put your trust in Him, and abandon the worship of others and looking to anything else. If you do not do so, He will punish you for that with the most severe and harshest punishment, for He, mighty and majestic, is severe in punishment. So know this and fear Him.

This is what the first verse [97] and the second [98] indicate. As for the third verse [99], it reaffirms the content of His saying in the second verse, ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, which is a stern warning. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to convey﴾, and he has conveyed; he warned and gave full notice, and the matter is now up to you. If you repent to your Lord and obey Him, He will forgive you and have mercy upon you, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. But if you turn away and disobey, He knows that from you, will hold you accountable for it and punish you for it, and He is severe in punishment. His saying ﴿And Allah knows what you show and what you conceal﴾ is both a promise and a warning, because His knowledge of the outward and the inward entails recompense: if the deed is good the recompense is good, and if the deed is evil the recompense is likewise.

This is the content of the third verse. As for the fourth [100], He, may He be exalted, says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say to the people, O people, that ﴿the corrupt is not equal﴾ in beliefs, sayings, deeds, men and wealth, ﴿nor the good﴾ among them, even if the abundance of the corrupt pleases you, that is, delights you. For the criterion is not quantity or scarcity, but the good that is beneficial and not harmful, even if it is little. Therefore, ﴿fear Allah, O people of understanding﴾, that is, fear Him, comply with His command, and avoid His prohibition, hoping that success will be attained for you by being saved from what is feared and by attaining what is desired and loved.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A statement of the great arrangement of Allah for His creation, for He secured the interests of Quraysh and the Arabs and produced for them safety and stability, followed by ease of life and good living, through the respect and veneration He placed in His servants for the Sacred House, the sacred month, the offerings and the garlands, a matter that none can achieve except Allah.

2- A statement of the Messenger's responsibility toward the people, that it is only conveying, and he, ﷺ, has conveyed.

3- Affirmation of the saying: the criterion is the quality, not the quantity. One believer is more beneficial than ten disbelievers, a lawful dirham is better than ten unlawful ones, and two accepted rak'ahs are better than ten that are not accepted.

4- The command to piety, in hope of the success of the God-fearing.

As for the third verse [99], it reaffirms the content of His saying in the second verse, ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾, which is a stern warning. So He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to convey﴾, and he has conveyed; he warned and gave full notice, and the matter is now up to you. If you repent to your Lord and obey Him, He will forgive you and have mercy upon you, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. But if you turn away and disobey, He knows that from you, will hold you accountable for it and punish you for it, and He is severe in punishment. His saying ﴿And Allah knows what you show and what you conceal﴾ is both a promise and a warning, because His knowledge of the outward and the inward entails recompense: if the deed is good the recompense is good, and if the deed is evil the recompense is likewise.

This is the content of the third verse. As for the fourth [100], He, may He be exalted, says to His Messenger ﷺ: Say to the people, O people, that ﴿the corrupt is not equal﴾ in beliefs, sayings, deeds, men and wealth, ﴿nor the good﴾ among them, even if the abundance of the corrupt pleases you, that is, delights you. 1- A statement of the great arrangement of Allah for His creation, for He secured the interests of Quraysh and the Arabs and produced for them safety and stability, followed by ease of life and good living, through the respect and veneration He placed in His servants for the Sacred House, the sacred month, the offerings and the garlands, a matter that none can achieve except Allah.

2- A statement of the Messenger's responsibility toward the people, that it is only conveying, and he, ﷺ, has conveyed.

3- Affirmation of the saying: the criterion is the quality, not the quantity. One believer is more beneficial than ten disbelievers, a lawful dirham is better than ten unlawful ones, and two accepted rak'ahs are better than ten that are not accepted.

"بحيرة ولا سائبة" (a bahirah or a sa'ibah): "البحيرة: الناقة تبحر أذنها أي تشق، والسائبة: الناقة تسيّب" (The bahirah is a she-camel whose ear is slit, and the sa'ibah is a she-camel that is set free).

"ولا وصيلة ولا حام" (nor a wasilah or a ham): "الوصيلة: الناقة يكون أول إنتاجها أنثى، والحام: الجمل يحمى ظهره للآلهة" (The wasilah is a she-camel whose first offspring is female, and the ham is a male camel whose back is protected for the idols).

"ما أنزل الله" (what God has sent down): "من الحق والخير" (of truth and goodness).

"ما وجدنا عليه آباءنا" (what we found our fathers upon): "من الباطل والضلال" (of falsehood and misguidance).

Meaning of the verses:

Some of the Companions asked the Messenger of God ﷺ so often that he became displeased with them. He stood up to address them and said: "«» Do not ask me today about anything except that I will make it clear to you." A man called Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, who, whenever he quarrelled with a man, would call him by other than his father's name, asked: "Who is my father, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Your father is Hudhafah."

Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ addressed us and said: "O people, God has enjoined upon you the Hajj, so perform it." A man said: "Is it every year, O Messenger of God?" He remained silent until the man asked three times. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "No. Had I said yes, it would have become obligatory, and had it become obligatory you would not have been able to do it." Then he said: "Leave me as I have left you." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were made apparent to you, would distress you﴾, meaning: if their answers were made apparent to you in response to your questions, you would be harmed and distressed by them. ﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made apparent to you﴾, meaning: our Messenger will explain them to you. As for asking about them before the Qur'an is revealed concerning them, that is not fitting for you, because it is a form of pressing upon the Messenger of God and harming him. Then God, exalted is He, said to them: ﴿God has pardoned that﴾, meaning: He did not hold you accountable for what you asked. ﴿And God is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾. So repent to Him and He will accept your repentance, and seek His forgiveness and He will forgive you and have mercy on you, for He is Forgiving and Merciful. The words of God, exalted is He: ﴿A people before you did ask such questions, and then they became disbelievers because of them﴾, meaning: a people before you asked these over-scrupulous, embarrassing questions of yours, ﴿and then they became disbelievers because of them﴾, because they were burdened with what they could not bear, and the requirement was hard upon them as a consequence of their obstinacy in asking their prophets, so they abandoned acting upon it and disbelieved. This is what the first verse [101] and the second [102] indicate. As for the third [103], God, exalted is He, said: ﴿God did not ordain any bahirah or sa'ibah or wasilah or ham﴾. It is possible that someone asked the Messenger about the bahirah and what follows it, so God revealed: ﴿God did not ordain any bahirah﴾, meaning: God did not slit the ear of a bahirah, nor set free a sa'ibah, nor link a wasilah, nor protect a hami. But those who disbelieve are the ones who did this, fabricating lies against God, ﴿and most of them do not reason﴾. Had they reasoned, they would not have fabricated against God, innovated, and legislated from themselves, attributing that to God, exalted is He. The first to set free the sawa'ib and alter the religion of Isma'il, peace be upon him, was Amr ibn Luhayy, whom the Messenger of God ﷺ saw dragging his intestines (qasab) in the Fire, that is, his bowels in Hell.

This is what the third verse contains. Then God, exalted is He, responded to them, rejecting their corrupt statement: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾, meaning: even if those fathers were ignorant and foolish, not understanding anything of the truth, and ﴿were not guided﴾ to any good or right.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Disapproval of persistent questioning, of probing into matters too deeply, and of over-scrupulousness in questions.

2- The prohibition of innovation in religion, and that it is the cause of the existence of shirk among people.

3- The obligation to refer matters of disagreement to the Book and the Sunnah and to accept their judgment.

4- The prohibition of blindly following ignorant people and following their falsehoods.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verse 105:

Explanation of the words:

Āmanū (those who believe): they affirmed Allah and His Messenger, and responded to them by doing what is commanded and abstaining from what is forbidden.

ʿAlaykum anfusakum (upon you is yourselves): bind yourselves to guiding and reforming them.

Idhā ihtadaytum (when you are guided): to knowledge of the truth and adherence to its path.

Ilā Llāhi marjiʿukum jamīʿan (to Allah is your return, all of you): both those who went astray and those who were guided.

Fa-yunabbiʾukum (so He will inform you): He will tell you of your deeds and recompense you for them.

Meaning of the noble verse:

Allah, exalted is He, calls His believing servants, saying: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, affirm belief in Allah and His Messenger, and in the promise and warning of Allah. ﴿Upon you is yourselves﴾: bind them to guidance and purity through faith and righteous deeds, and keep them away from polytheism and sins. ﴿Those who have gone astray will not harm you if you are guided﴾: that is, the misguidance of others does not harm you if you are guided, since ﴿no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾, ﴿every soul is recompensed for what it has earned, not for what another has earned﴾, and ﴿whoever is guided is only guided for his own soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment.﴾ However, among guidance is enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil. If the believers abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil, they are not considered guided, for by remaining silent about evil, it multiplies and spreads and inevitably leads to the believers going astray and losing their guidance. For this reason, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, once stood up to deliver a sermon and said: (O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves...etc.﴾ and you place it in other than its proper place. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When people see wrongdoing and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them with punishment.") His words, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ contain both promise and warning: a promise to those who obey Allah and His Messenger, and a warning to those who disobey them.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The obligation of the believer to reform himself and purify himself from the effects of polytheism and sins, through faith and righteous deeds.

2- The misguidance of people does not harm the believer if he enjoins what is good and forbids what is evil.

3- Affirmation of the principle of the Final Resurrection.

4- Deeds have the greatest effect on a person's happiness or misery.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 106–108:

Explanation of the words:

"Testimony between you" (shahadatu baynikum): shahada (testimony) is a statement issuing from knowledge acquired by sight or by insight; "between you" means the testimony of some of you concerning others.

"If you travel in the land" (in antum darabtum fi'l-ard): that is, if you are travelling.

"After the prayer" (min ba'di'l-salat): the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr).

"If you doubt" (in artabtum): if you suspect the truthfulness and integrity of their statement.

"If it is discovered" (fa-in 'uthira): that is, if it becomes known that they have betrayed what was entrusted to them to safeguard.

"Nearer" (adna): closer.

"In its proper form" (ala wajhiha): that is, correct as it is, with nothing lacking from it and nothing added to it.

"The defiantly disobedient" (al-fasiqin): those who do not commit themselves to obeying Allah and His Messenger in what they command and forbid.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to guide, instruct and direct the believers to that which perfects them and makes them happy. In these three verses [106], [107], [108], Allah, exalted is He, addresses His servant believers, saying: "O you who have believed, let there be [the] testimony between you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest: two just men from among you" (i.e., let two just men from among the Muslims witness the bequest of one of you when death approaches him), "or two others from other than you" (i.e., from non-Muslims), "if you are travelling in the land and the disaster of death strikes you." If you doubt the truthfulness of their report and the soundness of their testimony, then detain them, that is, stop them after the afternoon prayer in the mosque, so that they swear to you by Allah, saying: "By Allah, we will not exchange our oath for a small price, even if it concerns a relative," and "we will not conceal the testimony of Allah; for then we would indeed be among the sinners." "And if it is discovered that the two had committed a sin" (i.e., if it is found that those who witnessed the bequest and swore to its truth have betrayed it, or lied in what they swore to), "then two others shall take their place from among those who have been wronged" by the two, who will swear by Allah, saying: "By Allah, our testimony is more deserving than theirs," i.e., our oaths are more truthful and sound than theirs. "And we have not transgressed" against them with a false accusation, for if we did that we would be among the wrongdoers. When they swear this oath, they are entitled to what they swore to, and what the two witnesses of the bequest had withheld and denied at the time of death is returned to the heirs of the deceased.

He, exalted is He, says: "That is nearer to their giving the testimony in its proper form" — that is, closer to their bringing the testimony just, without partiality or injustice. His words "or they fear that oaths will be rejected after their oaths" mean: and it is closer to their fearing that counter-oaths will be returned against them, so that they do not lie out of fear of disgrace. His words "And fear Allah" mean: fear Him, O believers, and do not depart from His obedience. "And listen" to what you are commanded and respond to Allah in it. Indeed, Allah does not guide to the path of good and perfection the defiantly disobedient who depart from His obedience, so beware of defiance and avoid it.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of bequest both at home and while travelling, and encouragement and exhortation to it.

2- The obligation of calling witnesses to a bequest.

3- The testimony of a non-Muslim concerning a bequest is permissible when a Muslim cannot be found.

4- The recommendation of swearing after the afternoon prayer, to emphasize the seriousness of the oath.

5- The legitimacy of administering an oath to witnesses when the judge doubts them or suspects their truthfulness.

**Ayyadtuka** (I strengthened you): I empowered you and gave you victory.

**Bi-ruh al-qudus** (with the Holy Spirit): Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him.

**Al-mahd** (the cradle): the bed of an infant.

**Al-kahl** (the middle-aged man): one who has passed the age of youth, that is, thirty years.

**Al-kitab** (the writing): the script and the act of writing.

**Al-hikmah** (wisdom): understanding the secrets of the Shari'ah and being correct in all matters.

**Takhluqu ka-hay'ati al-tayr** (you shape from clay the likeness of a bird): that is, you bring into being and fashion a form like the shape of a bird.

**Al-akmah wa al-abras** (the blind from birth and the leper): *al-akmah* is one born blind, and *al-abras* is one afflicted with leprosy.

**Tukhriju al-mawta** (you bring forth the dead): that is, alive from their graves.

**Kaffaftu** (I restrained): that is, I prevented.

**Meaning of the Verses**

Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, warns His believing servants about the terrors of the final resurrection, the Day when He gathers the messengers (peace be upon them) and questions them, while He is most knowing of them: ﴿So He will say, "What response did you receive?"﴾ Did your nations obey you or disobey you? Then they will be confounded and bewildered, and will entrust the matter to Him, the Exalted, saying: ﴿We have no knowledge; indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ If this is the state of the messengers, how much more so the state of those below them among the people.

Allah singles out Jesus (peace be upon him) among the messengers to be addressed in this great station, because two great nations went astray concerning him: the Jews claimed that he was a sorcerer and the son of adultery, and the Christians claimed that he was God and the son of God. So Allah addresses him while they listen: ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother.﴾ You are My servant and My messenger, and your mother is My handmaiden. He then mentions to him the kinds of His blessings upon him, saying: ﴿when I supported you with the Holy Spirit,﴾ that is, Jibril (peace be upon him), ﴿you spoke to the people in the cradle﴾ while you were a child. Then the Children of Israel said, "Revive for us Sam ibn Nuh," so he stood at his grave and called out to him, and he rose alive from his grave while they watched. Remember ﴿when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs,﴾ so they disbelieved you and intended to kill you and crucify you. ﴿But those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but clear magic."﴾ Remember ﴿when I inspired the disciples through your tongue, [saying], "Believe in Me and My Messenger,"﴾ that is, in you, O Jesus. ﴿They said, "We have believed; bear witness that we are Muslims,"﴾ that is, submitting and obedient to what you command us, from the obedience to our Lord and obedience to you.

Remember ﴿when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs,﴾ so they disbelieved you and intended to kill you and crucify you. ﴿But those who disbelieved among them said, "This is not but clear magic."﴾ Remember ﴿when I inspired the disciples through your tongue, [saying], "Believe in Me and My Messenger,"﴾ that is, in you, O Jesus. ﴿They said, "We have believed; bear witness that we are Muslims,"﴾ that is, submitting and obedient to what you command us, from the obedience to our Lord and obedience to you.

**Guidance from the Verses**

1. The terror of the Day of Resurrection and the severity of that station, to the extent that even the messengers will be bewildered.
2. The obligation to prepare for that Day by being mindful of Allah, the Exalted.
3. The rebuke of the Jews and Christians: the Jews' neglect regarding Jesus and the Christians' exaggeration concerning him.
4. The demonstration of Allah's honouring of Jesus and the grace and favours He bestowed upon him.
5. The establishment and affirmation of the miracles of Jesus (peace be upon him).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 112–115:

Explanation of the words:

"Can your Lord send down to us a table (ma'idah) from heaven?" — "Can" here means: Will He obey and consent?

"A table from the heaven": al-ma'idah is the spread (khiwan) and what is placed upon it, or the food itself; the intended meaning here is the food.

"And our hearts be at rest": that is, be settled through an increase of certainty within them.

"And we be among its witnesses": that is, we bear witness that it came down from heaven.

"A festival ('id)": that is, a day that returns to us every year, on which we remember God Most High and give Him thanks.

"And a sign from You": a sign from You of Your power and Your mercy, and of the prophethood of Your Prophet.

"Whoever among you disbelieves after this": whoever among you disbelieves after the table has been sent down, O you who asked for the table.

"Any one of the worlds": that is, any one of all mankind.

Meaning of the verses:

God Most High says to His servant and messenger Jesus: Remember when "I inspired the disciples: Believe in Me and in My Messenger. They said: We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims" [al-Ma'idah 5:111]. "When the disciples said": "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Since this statement indicated doubt in their souls and a lack of certainty about their Lord's power, Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: "Fear God, if you are believers," so do not say such a thing. Then they made excuses for their false words: "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be at rest, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses" — that it came down from heaven by your asking your Lord for it. Here Jesus, peace be upon him, called upon his Lord, humbly and submissively: "O God" — that is, O Allah — "our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven that will be a festival for us, for the first of us" — that is, for those of us present now — "and the last of us" — that is, for those who come after us — "and a sign from You," that is, a sign from You of Your oneness and Your great power, and of my truthfulness in Your sending me as a messenger to the Children of Israel. "And provide for us" — and bestow upon us Your provision and Your bounty — "for You are the best of providers." God answered him, saying: "I will indeed send it down upon you." And indeed He sent it down. "Whoever among you disbelieves after this," O Children of Israel who asked for the table, by denying My oneness, or the mission of My messenger, or My great power, "then I will punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds." Therefore, those among them who disbelieved were transformed into apes and swine.

1. The harshness, arrogance, and bad manners of the Jews toward their prophets, as when they said to Moses: "So go you and your Lord and fight; we will sit here" [al-Ma'idah 5:24], and said to Jesus: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?"

3. The legitimacy of religious festivals for worshipping God through prayer and remembrance, in thanks to God Most High; in Islam there are two festivals: al-Adha (al-Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice) and al-Fitr (al-Fitr, the Festival of Breaking the Fast).

4. Among the people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the family of Pharaoh, the hypocrites, and those among the people of the table who disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 5, verses 116–120:

Explanation of the words:

*Ilahayn* (two gods): two objects of worship besides Me.

*Subhanaka* (glory be to You): exalting You and declaring You free of imperfection.

*Ma yakunu li* (it is not for me): it is not fitting for me, nor is it possible for me to do that.

*Shahidan* (witness): watchful over them.

*Al-Raqib* (the Watchful): the Guardian, the Preserver.

*In tu'adhdhibhum* (if You punish them): that is, with Your fire, for they are Your servants and You do with them as You will.

*Wa in taghfir lahum* (and if You forgive them): that is, You cover over them and show them mercy by admitting them to Your Paradise.

*Al-'Aziz al-Hakim* (the Mighty, the Wise): *al-'Aziz* is the Overpowering whom nothing can prevent from attaining His will; *al-Hakim* is the One who places everything in its proper place, so He sends the polytheist to the Fire and the monotheist to the Garden.

*Al-Sadiqin* (the truthful): plural of *sadiq*, one who is truthful toward his Lord in worshipping Him alone.

*Wa radu 'anhu* (and they are pleased with Him): because He rewards them for their deeds with gardens beneath which rivers flow.

*Ala kulli shay'in qadir* (over all things capable): that is, over doing anything upon which His will is set and which He wishes to do; He does it and nothing can ever overpower Him in any circumstance.

Meaning of the verses:

God Most High says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "Mention to your people" ﴿And when God said﴾ on the Day when He gathers the Messengers and asks them, "What answer were you given?", and He questions Jesus alone, rebuking the Christians for their polytheism: ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God"?﴾ That is, two objects of worship. He establishes this for them, and Jesus immediately denies it, exalting his Lord and declaring Him holy, saying: ﴿Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what is not mine by right.﴾ He affirms his innocence of what he was charged with, rebuking his people: ﴿If I had said it, You would have known it.﴾ O my Lord, You know what is in my soul, so how much more what I say and do; and I do not know what is in Your essence, unless You inform me of something, for ﴿You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ ﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me﴾ to say to them, which is ﴿Worship God, my Lord and your Lord, and I was a witness over them﴾, that is, a watcher. ﴿But when You took me up﴾ by raising me to You, ﴿You were the Watcher over them﴾, observing their deeds and preserving them for them so that You may recompense them for them. ﴿And You are a Witness over all things.﴾ Watcher and Preserver. ﴿If You punish them﴾, that is, whoever among them died in polytheism, by casting him into Your Fire, then You are capable of that, ﴿and if You forgive them﴾, that is, whoever died in monotheism, by admitting him into Your Garden, for he is worthy of that; for You are ﴿the Mighty﴾, overpowering in Your affair, ﴿the Wise﴾, who places everything in its proper place, so He does not bestow favor upon one who associates others with Him, nor punish one who obeyed Him and affirmed His oneness. The Lord, blessed and exalted, answered, saying: ﴿This is a day when the truthfulness of the truthful will benefit them.﴾ They were truthful toward God Most High in their faith, worshipping Him alone without partner and not associating anything with Him. Its benefit to them is that they are admitted by it into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, never leaving them, together with God's pleasure with them and their pleasure with Him, for what He bestowed upon them of bliss that never ends nor perishes. ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾ It is deliverance from the Fire and entrance into the Gardens. In the last verse [120], He informs that to Him belongs ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them﴾ of all creatures and beings, by creation, ownership and disposal; He does in them whatever He wills, so He shows mercy and punishes, ﴿and He is capable of all things.﴾ Nothing can overpower Him in the earth or in the heaven, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Rebuke of the Christians on the Plains of Judgment for deifying Jesus and his mother, peace be upon them both.

2. The innocence of Jesus, peace be upon him, from the polytheist Christians and the People of the Book.

3. The punishment of polytheists and the bliss of monotheists rests upon the principle of divine wisdom.

4. The virtue of truthfulness, and that it benefits in this world and the Hereafter. In the hadith: "Hold to truthfulness, for it leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to speak the truth and seek it until he is written before God as a *siddiq* (one who is truly truthful)."

5. Asking anything from other than God is a form of falsehood and polytheism, for other than God owns nothing; and one who owns nothing, how can he give, and from where can he give?
